#### To install Bun

{% codetabs %}

```sh#curl
$ curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
```

```sh#npm
$ npm install -g bun
```

```sh#powershell
$ powershell -c "irm bun.sh/install.ps1|iex"
```

```sh#scoop
$ scoop install bun
```

```sh#brew
$ brew tap oven-sh/bun
$ brew install bun
```

```sh#docker
$ docker pull oven/bun
$ docker run --rm --init --ulimit memlock=-1:-1 oven/bun
```

{% /codetabs %}

#### To upgrade Bun

```sh
$ bun upgrade
```

## `bun fmt`: a formatter built into Bun

`bun fmt` is an incredibly fast, Prettier-compatible code formatter that works with your existing Prettier or oxfmt config.

```sh
$ bun fmt
src/index.ts
src/styles.css
Formatted 2 files, 2 unchanged [5.59ms]
```

It formats JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, Flow, CSS, SCSS, Less, HTML, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Lightning Web Components, MJML, JSON, JSONC, JSON5, YAML, TOML, Markdown, MDX, GraphQL and Handlebars. Embedded code is formatted too, like `<style>` in HTML, code blocks in Markdown and `` css`...` `` templates in JavaScript.

In Prettier's own repository (2,616 files, with their config), `bun fmt --check` takes 60 ms and Prettier takes 17 seconds:

| Tool            |    Time | Peak memory |
| --------------- | ------: | ----------: |
| `bun fmt`       | 59.7 ms |       48 MB |
| Prettier 3.9.10 |  17.1 s |      459 MB |

That's 286x faster. On vitest, date-fns, monkeytype and h3, it's 234x to 425x faster than Prettier 3.9.9.

On projects that already use oxfmt, with their own config, it's 3x to 6x faster than oxfmt 0.74.0:

| Project     | Files | `bun fmt` | oxfmt 0.74.0 | Faster |       Memory |
| ----------- | ----: | --------: | -----------: | -----: | -----------: |
| RSSHub      | 7,121 |   97.3 ms |     298.5 ms |   3.0x |  42 vs 95 MB |
| redocly-cli | 3,397 |   62.4 ms |     217.5 ms |   3.4x | 61 vs 107 MB |
| vite        | 2,537 |   65.2 ms |     406.7 ms |   6.2x | 64 vs 137 MB |
| fumadocs    | 2,452 |   44.6 ms |     1,395 ms |    31x | 48 vs 179 MB |

Both tools see the same files, exit 0 and leave the tree unchanged.

{% details summary="Reproduce these numbers" %}

Each project is a fresh clone at a pinned commit. The oxfmt projects have no `node_modules`.

```sh#vite
$ bun install -g oxfmt@0.74.0
$ git clone https://github.com/vitejs/vite && cd vite
$ git checkout 4ca25e1d3a24
$ hyperfine --warmup 2 "oxfmt ." "bun fmt ."
```

```sh#redocly-cli
$ git clone https://github.com/Redocly/redocly-cli && cd redocly-cli
$ git checkout 82da67d6ea5b
$ hyperfine --warmup 3 --runs 20 "oxfmt --check ." "bun fmt --check ."
```

```sh#RSSHub
$ git clone https://github.com/DIYgod/RSSHub && cd RSSHub
$ git checkout 8776927c78de
$ hyperfine --warmup 3 --runs 20 "oxfmt --check ." "bun fmt --check ."
```

```sh#fumadocs
$ git clone https://github.com/fuma-nama/fumadocs && cd fumadocs
$ git checkout bc86bbb0d406
$ hyperfine --warmup 3 --runs 20 "oxfmt --check ." "bun fmt --check ."
```

```sh#prettier
$ git clone https://github.com/prettier/prettier && cd prettier
$ git checkout df39b5b60a28
$ bun install --ignore-scripts
$ hyperfine --warmup 3 "bun fmt --no-script . --check" "node node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs . --check"
```

The same runs on one core, and on only vite's JavaScript and TypeScript files (`'**/*.{js,mjs,cjs,jsx,ts,mts,cts,tsx}'`):

| Run                         | `bun fmt` | oxfmt 0.74.0 | Faster |
| --------------------------- | --------: | -----------: | -----: |
| vite, 1,608 JS and TS files |   52.2 ms |     188.3 ms |   3.6x |
| RSSHub, one core            |  621.6 ms |     1,212 ms |   1.9x |
| redocly-cli, one core       |  375.1 ms |     645.5 ms |   1.7x |
| fumadocs, one core          |  255.2 ms |     5,608 ms |    21x |

- vite: 16-core M4 Max MacBook Pro, macOS 26.7. Mean.
- Everything else: Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C, 8 physical cores pinned with `taskset`, Amazon Linux 2023, xfs on NVMe, warm file cache. Median.

{% /details %}

`bun fmt` wouldn't exist without [Prettier](https://github.com/prettier/prettier), [Biome](https://github.com/biomejs/biome) and [Oxc](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc). It's a port of Prettier, and the JavaScript and TypeScript printer is a port of [`oxc_formatter`](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/tree/main/crates/oxc_formatter), which is a port of Biome's formatter.

Thank you to the Prettier, Biome and Oxc teams for years of great work.

Read more in the [docs](/docs/format).

### `bun fmt --check`

`--check` lists the files that need formatting without writing anything. It exits with code 1 if there are any.

```sh
$ bun fmt --check
src/index.ts
src/styles.css
2 files need formatting. Run bun fmt to fix them.
```

### `bun fmt --staged` and `--changed`

`--staged` only formats the files you're about to commit and re-stages them, so you don't need `lint-staged`.

```sh#.git/hooks/pre-commit
#!/bin/sh
bun fmt --staged
```

`--changed` formats the files that differ from your default branch. Pass a ref to compare against something else.

```sh
$ bun fmt --changed
$ bun fmt --changed=origin/dev
```

### Use your Prettier or oxfmt config

`bun fmt` reads `.prettierrc*`, `prettier.config.*`, `"prettier"` in `package.json`, `overrides`, `.editorconfig` and `.prettierignore`. It also reads `.oxfmtrc.json`, `.oxfmtrc.jsonc` and `oxfmt.config.ts` (or `.mts`). It accepts the same CLI flags as Prettier or oxfmt, and `// prettier-ignore` comments work.

```json-diff
  "scripts": {
-   "format": "prettier --write ."
+   "format": "bun fmt"
  }
```

Import sorting is built in, so you can leave `@trivago/prettier-plugin-sort-imports`, `@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports` and `prettier-plugin-organize-imports` in `plugins`. Languages that need a Prettier plugin, like Astro, fall back to the Prettier installed in your project.

The command is `bun fmt`, like `cargo fmt`, `go fmt`, `deno fmt` and `zig fmt`. `bun format` still runs your `format` script.

`bun fmt --doctor` shows how Bun interprets your config and which packages you can uninstall.

### Options in `bunfig.toml`

All of Prettier's options are supported under the same names. Each one is also available as a flag, like `--print-width 100` or `--no-semi`. `bun fmt --init` creates the `[fmt]` section.

```toml#bunfig.toml
[fmt]
printWidth = 100
semi = false
sortImports = true
sortTailwindcss = true
sortPackageJson = true
jsdoc = true

[[fmt.overrides]]
files = ["*.test.ts"]
options = { printWidth = 120 }
```

`sortImports`, `sortTailwindcss`, `sortPackageJson` and `jsdoc` are off by default, and don't need a Prettier or oxfmt config. `sortImports` groups imports, sorts the names in `{ }` and merges duplicate imports from the same module.

In a monorepo, `bun fmt` walks up from the working directory to the nearest `bunfig.toml` with a `[fmt]` section. Without a Prettier config, `bun fmt` also formats TOML. It skips `*.min.js`, `*.min.css` and lockfiles unless you pass them explicitly.

### Prettier's Tailwind, `package.json` and Svelte plugins are built in

`bun fmt` does the work of `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss`, `prettier-plugin-packagejson` and `prettier-plugin-svelte`, so you don't need them installed. You can leave them in `plugins`, and their options are supported.

```tsx
// Before
<button className="text-white px-4 sm:px-8 py-2 bg-sky-700 hover:bg-sky-800" />
// After
<button className="bg-sky-700 px-4 py-2 text-white hover:bg-sky-800 sm:px-8" />
```

Tailwind classes are sorted with your project's `tailwindcss`, version 3 or 4. If it isn't installed, they're left as they are.

We compared the output against Prettier 3.9.9 with version 0.8.1 of the plugin, on Tailwind 4.3.3 and 3.4.19.

| Input                                                                        |  Total | Identical |     % |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -----: | --------: | ----: |
| JavaScript and TypeScript files                                              | 13,952 |    13,654 | 97.9% |
| HTML, Vue, Angular, LWC, Handlebars, CSS, SCSS, Less, Markdown and MDX files |  2,176 |     2,148 | 98.7% |
| Tailwind 3 projects                                                          |     15 |        15 |  100% |

About half of the differences are intentional. In `` className={`header${open ? " active" : ""}`} ``, the plugin trims `" active"` to `"active"`, so the element ends up with the class `headeractive`. `bun fmt` keeps the space.

For `package.json`, keys are sorted in the same order as the plugin and values are left untouched. Of 13,670 real-world `package.json` files, 13,644 (99.8%) are byte-for-byte identical to the output of Prettier 3.9.9 with the plugin. 20 differ only in values that Bun preserves, and the plugin throws on the other 6.

`.svelte` files are formatted by default, and the output matches `prettier-plugin-svelte` 4.1.1. With a Prettier config, they're formatted if the config lists the plugin. To skip them, set `svelte = false` in `[fmt]` or pass `--no-svelte`.

If your config uses a plugin that `bun fmt` doesn't support, like `prettier-plugin-jsdoc`, it prints an error naming the plugin, skips the files the plugin applies to and exits with code 2.

### Where `bun fmt` intentionally differs from Prettier

Prettier's output changes the meaning of the code for these inputs. `bun fmt` preserves it.

| Input                                          | Prettier 3.9.9                                       | `bun fmt` |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `font-family: Font\ Awesome` in CSS            | `Font\Awesome`, where `\A` is a hex escape           | Kept      |
| `x \|b` in a CSS selector                      | `x\|b`, a namespace selector instead of a descendant | Kept      |
| `<!DOCTYPE html>` in Handlebars                | Dropped                                              | Kept      |
| A `<script>` with a `// comment` in Handlebars | Lines joined, so the comment swallows the next line  | Kept      |

`bun fmt --debug-check` re-parses each file after formatting and fails if the meaning changed, like Prettier's `--debug-check`.

### Testing `bun fmt`

Bun's CI runs Prettier 3.9.9's own formatting tests on every commit. A test passes when the output is byte-for-byte identical to Prettier's.

64 of the 83 differences are one intentional case: Prettier drops trailing blank lines from a YAML block scalar, which changes the string.

| Language        |     Tests | Identical |         % |
| --------------- | --------: | --------: | --------: |
| JavaScript      |     1,357 |     1,356 |     99.9% |
| JSX             |       186 |       186 |      100% |
| TypeScript      |       756 |       756 |      100% |
| Flow            |     1,505 |     1,503 |     99.9% |
| JSON            |       785 |       785 |      100% |
| CSS             |       162 |       160 |     98.8% |
| Less            |       238 |       236 |     99.2% |
| SCSS            |       136 |       135 |     99.3% |
| GraphQL         |       104 |       102 |     98.1% |
| YAML            |     1,621 |     1,554 |     95.9% |
| Markdown        |     1,572 |     1,569 |     99.8% |
| MDX             |        32 |        32 |      100% |
| HTML            |       272 |       269 |     98.9% |
| Vue             |       189 |       189 |      100% |
| Angular         |       109 |       109 |      100% |
| Handlebars      |       128 |       128 |      100% |
| MJML, LWC, misc |       579 |       579 |      100% |
| **Total**       | **9,731** | **9,648** | **99.1%** |

Another 90 tests are skipped. 66 of them use syntax proposals at stage 2 or below that only Babel parses, and 13 need a Prettier plugin.

With an oxfmt config, `bun fmt` matches oxfmt 0.72's output on 1,343 of oxfmt's 1,498 fixtures (89.7%).

On 330 open-source repositories, we ran each project's format command with its own formatter and with `bun fmt`. A run only counts as identical if every file is byte-for-byte the same. Next.js counts as a mismatch: 26,334 files are identical, but `bun fmt` rejects one file that uses a Babel-only proposal.

| Compared with | Runs | Identical |     % |
| ------------- | ---: | --------: | ----: |
| oxfmt 0.72    |  240 |       227 | 94.6% |
| Prettier      |   74 |        57 | 77.0% |

Most of the Prettier mismatches come from an older version of Prettier, Prettier plugins or Markdown files.

## New in `bun check`

### `bun check` is 1.4x to 7.8x faster on large projects

Cold runs with 8 threads on a Linux x64 machine, best of 3. Both versions report the same number of errors on each project.

| Project           | Bun v1.4.4 | Bun v1.4.3 | Faster |
| ----------------- | ---------: | ---------: | -----: |
| MUI `docs`        |     1.31 s |    10.28 s |   7.8x |
| t3code `server`   |     1.62 s |     4.59 s |   2.8x |
| Supabase `studio` |     1.27 s |     2.84 s |   2.2x |
| mikro-orm         |     1.82 s |     3.30 s |   1.8x |
| VS Code           |     2.82 s |     4.09 s |   1.4x |

Peak memory on MUI's `docs` drops from 11.2 GB to 1.3 GB. The other four use up to 0.3 GB more.

Of 76 other repositories, 69 are more than 10% faster. Bun's own `src/js` is slower: 0.20 s, up from 0.11 s.

- A `switch` with thousands of cases, or a variable with thousands of assignments that's read from closures, no longer takes seconds to check.
- On Windows, files load 31% to 45% faster in projects with an isolated install. That's 50 to 100 ms per run on opencode's packages.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/6bb5dc1956505dd1113455f58d4757c924f3ad54 -->

### `bun check -b` is up to 15x faster with many projects

With `bun check -b`, projects share parsed declaration files, module resolution caches and the list of emitted files. Each project used to keep its own copy, so check time grew much faster than the number of projects.

`bun check -b` on generated monorepos with `skipLibCheck: true`, best of 6 runs on a 16-core M4 Max:

| Monorepo                                                  | Bun v1.4.4 | Bun v1.4.3 | Faster |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------: | ---------: | -----: |
| 1,000 independent projects, 5 files each                  |     0.53 s |     2.07 s |   3.9x |
| 4,000 independent projects, 5 files each                  |     0.87 s |    13.65 s |  15.7x |
| 800 projects with up to 40 references each, 20 files each |     1.26 s |     7.36 s |   5.8x |

In the last one, peak memory dropped from 1,987 MB to 872 MB.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/788087c0a4e0c4e57dfe78156ba57a70e329d1b1 -->

## New in `bun install`

### `bun install` migrates Yarn Berry lockfiles

`bun install` converts a Yarn 2+ (Berry) `yarn.lock` to `bun.lock` and preserves every pinned version. Bun v1.4.3 only migrated Yarn v1 lockfiles, so switching a Berry project to Bun re-resolved every dependency.

```sh
$ bun install
bun install v1.4.4
[59.59ms] migrated lockfile from yarn.lock
```

- Workspaces, `npm:` aliases, `resolutions`, and git, tarball and `file:` dependencies are preserved.
- `patch:` dependencies become `patchedDependencies` in `package.json`.
- `catalog:` ranges are read from `.yarnrc.yml`. The catalogs are copied into `package.json`.

The migration is all-or-nothing. If Bun can't preserve everything `yarn.lock` pins, it prints the reason and falls back to resolving from `package.json`. For example:

- An `exec:` dependency.
- A registry set in `.yarnrc.yml` but not in `bunfig.toml` or `.npmrc`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/d1cb7db55a7b226c6ffbb876cfef635fe4959357 -->

### `bun install` retries with exponential backoff

`bun install` retries failed requests up to five times. In Bun v1.4.3, all five retries happened within 5 ms, so a brief registry outage would fail the install.

Now it waits 50 ms before the first retry and doubles the delay each time: 50, 100, 200, 400 and 800 ms, with ±20% jitter.

Installing one package from a misbehaving registry, and how long the command took:

| Registry           |    Bun v1.4.4 |   Bun v1.4.3 |
| ------------------ | ------------: | -----------: |
| One 503, then OK   |  works, 78 ms | works, 22 ms |
| 503 for 100 ms     | works, 222 ms |  fails, 8 ms |
| 503 or 429 for 1 s |  works, 1.6 s |  fails, 7 ms |
| 503 for 3 s        |  fails, 1.5 s | fails, 18 ms |
| Nothing listening  |  fails, 1.6 s | fails, 15 ms |

To tolerate outages longer than 1.5 seconds, increase the initial delay:

```sh
# waits 250 ms, 500 ms, 1 s, 2 s and 4 s
$ BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_RETRY_BACKOFF=250 bun install
```

- `BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_RETRY_BACKOFF=0` retries immediately, like before.
- `Retry-After` headers are respected, up to 60 seconds.
- 429 and 408 responses are retried.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/8ba82c36d62d7fb42df72baf53c71b04db0f6d40 -->

### 133 `bun install` issues closed

We had 597 open package manager pull requests. 464 landed in full and 40 landed partially.

Every one of these PRs had tests that failed in the previous version of Bun and now pass. This nearly doubled bun install's test suite.

We also fuzzed it:

- We compared the old and new versions on 600 generated projects covering every kind of dependency, both linkers and both lockfile formats.
- We ran 7 commands against 90,000 mutated `bun.lockb` files without a crash or hang.
- We compared version selection against `npm-pick-manifest` on 200,000 generated cases. It differs in two: a `latest` tag that points to a missing version, and `^1.0.0-a.0`.

### Hoisted installs from a warm cache are up to 3.2x faster on Linux

The hoisted linker links packages on up to 8 threads on macOS and Linux. It helps most when the cache is warm and `node_modules` is missing or incomplete, like a CI job that restores Bun's cache.

{% image src="/images/hoisted-linker-1.4.4.svg" width="640" height="418" alt="Animation, in 50x slow motion, of bun install filling node_modules for a create-t3-app project. In Bun v1.4.4, folders like @trpc/server, drizzle-orm, next and zod are linked in parallel, and the install takes 91 ms. In Bun v1.4.3, the same folders are linked one at a time, and it takes 162 ms. Bun v1.4.4 is 1.8x faster." caption="create-t3-app, 102 packages, warm cache, Linux" /%}

Installing 1,000 packages with 30 files each on Linux, with everything already cached:

| `node_modules` | CPU cores |  After | Before |
| -------------- | --------: | -----: | -----: |
| Empty          |         8 | 120 ms | 381 ms |
| Empty          |         4 | 174 ms | 383 ms |
| Empty          |         2 | 162 ms | 222 ms |
| Half installed |         8 |  54 ms | 140 ms |
| Half installed |         4 |  65 ms | 174 ms |
| Half installed |         2 | 107 ms | 161 ms |

### Linux installs skip native packages built for the other libc

Packages like `sharp`, `@swc/core`, `lightningcss` and `rollup` publish one optional dependency per platform, and mark each Linux build with `"libc": ["glibc"]` or `"libc": ["musl"]`. Bun previously ignored that field, so every Linux install downloaded both builds. Now it only installs the one that matches your system, like npm and pnpm.

```sh
$ bun install --libc musl # for an Alpine image, from a glibc machine
$ bun install --libc '*'  # both builds, like before
```

The field is saved in `bun.lock`. Lockfiles written by older versions of Bun don't have it, so existing packages pick it up when they're updated or when you regenerate the lockfile.

### Peer dependencies resolve more like pnpm

When nothing in your project provides a package's peer dependency, Bun installs a version that satisfies the peer range. Before, the package got whatever version an unrelated package happened to install.

```json#package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "1.20.0",
    "@remix-run/express": "2.17.1"
  }
}
```

`@remix-run/express` has a peer dependency on `express@^4.20.0`. The MCP SDK depends on `express@5`.

| Version    | `@remix-run/express` gets                                |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bun v1.4.4 | `express@4`                                              |
| Bun v1.4.3 | `express@5`, with an `incorrect peer dependency` warning |

Installing `elysia` alongside `@jest/schemas` had the same problem: `elysia` got `@sinclair/typebox@0.27` and failed to load.

How `bun install` picks a peer dependency's version:

1. If your project, the workspace or any ancestor of the package depends on the peer, that version is used, even if it's out of range. With `react@17` in your app, every library it uses gets `react@17`.
2. Otherwise, every package with that peer dependency shares a single version that satisfies all of them. Bun prefers a version that's already installed, then the newest one in the registry.
3. If no single version satisfies all of them, Bun still avoids installing one copy per package, because packages like `react` and `graphql` break when two copies are loaded. Each package uses an installed version in its range if there is one, and otherwise shares the version the others use.

When an install has to resolve dependencies, `--verbose` prints every peer dependency that ended up out of range.

Versions already in `bun.lock` don't change. To re-resolve a peer, remove the package that needs it and add it back.

`bun update --latest` only needs to run once. In Bun v1.4.3, updating `react-dom@17` to `react-dom@19` changed its peer range, but a `react` that was only installed as its peer stayed on 17 until the second run.

### `bun pm fetch`

`bun pm fetch` downloads every dependency into the cache and nothing else. It doesn't create `node_modules`, run scripts or touch the lockfile.

In a Dockerfile, this keeps the downloads in a layer that's only rebuilt when `package.json` or `bun.lock` changes:

```dockerfile#Dockerfile
COPY package.json bun.lock ./
RUN bun pm fetch

COPY . .
RUN bun install --offline --frozen-lockfile
```

In a monorepo, the first step only needs the root `package.json` and the lockfile.

### `bun pm cache pack`, `unpack` and `prune`

`pack` writes the cache entries your lockfile needs into a single file, and `unpack` restores them on another machine.

```sh
# after an install
$ bun pm cache pack .ci/bun-cache.pack

# on another runner, before the install
$ bun pm cache unpack .ci/bun-cache.pack
$ bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

`unpack` only adds what's missing, and rejects a corrupted pack entirely.

`prune` removes old packages from the cache without clearing all of it:

```sh
$ bun pm cache prune             # older than 30 days
$ bun pm cache prune --max-age 7 # older than 7 days
$ bun pm cache prune --dry-run   # list what would go
```

### `bun publish --recursive` and `--filter`

Publish every package in a monorepo with one command. Dependencies are published before the packages that depend on them.

```sh
$ bun publish --recursive --quiet
skipped acme: private
skipped @acme/core@1.2.0: already on the registry
skipped @acme/docs: private

@acme/ui
Tag: latest
Access: default
Registry: https://registry.npmjs.org/

 + @acme/ui@1.2.0
```

- `--filter "@acme/*"` only publishes matching workspaces.
- Private packages and versions already on the registry are skipped, so it's safe to re-run after a failure.
- Every package is packed before the first one is published.

### `packageExtensions`

Some packages import a dependency they never declare, which fails with isolated installs. `packageExtensions` in the root `package.json` adds the missing entry without a fork or a patch.

```json#package.json
{
  "packageExtensions": {
    "legacy-plugin@2": {
      "dependencies": { "lodash": "^4.17.21" }
    },
    "react-redux@7": {
      "peerDependencies": { "react": "*" }
    }
  }
}
```

It uses the same format as pnpm and Yarn, and Bun copies the setting over when it migrates a `pnpm-lock.yaml` or `yarn.lock`.

### `link:` supports paths

`link:./dir` symlinks a directory into `node_modules`, like in Yarn and pnpm. The path is relative to the `package.json` that declares it. You don't need to run `bun link` first.

```json#package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "design-tokens": "link:./vendor/design-tokens",
    "shared": "link:../shared"
  }
}
```

`link:shared`, without a path, still refers to a package registered with `bun link`.

### `bun install` warns about deprecated packages

```sh
$ bun add rimraf@3
warn: deprecated rimraf@3.0.2: Rimraf versions prior to v4 are no longer supported
```

Deprecated direct dependencies each print one line. `--verbose` also lists transitive ones.

Like npm, Bun prefers non-deprecated versions when resolving a range, and `bun add pkg` skips a deprecated `latest`. Versions already in `bun.lock` don't change until you run `bun update`.

### `minimumReleaseAge` supports units and per-version exclusions

```toml#bunfig.toml
[install]
minimumReleaseAge = "3d" # also "90m", "12 hours", "2 weeks"
minimumReleaseAgeExcludes = ["@types/bun", "typescript@5.9.3"]
```

A plain number is still interpreted as seconds. `name@version` excludes a single release, like a security fix you need today, while the rest of that package's versions still have to wait.

Both are also available as flags: `--minimum-release-age 3d` and the new `--minimum-release-age-excludes typescript@5.9.3`.

### `--env-file` for the package manager, and new `bunx` flags

```sh
$ bun install --env-file ci.env
$ bunx --env-file ci.env prisma migrate deploy
$ bunx --cwd packages/api prisma migrate deploy
```

`bun install --env-file ci.env` used to try to install a package named `ci.env`.

- `--env-file <file>`, `--no-env-file` and `env = false` in `bunfig.toml` work with every package manager command.
- `bunx --cwd <dir>` runs the tool in another directory.
- `bunx --minimum-release-age <seconds>` applies the minimum release age to packages that `bunx` downloads.
- `bunx --trust` runs lifecycle scripts for the package and all of its dependencies.

### `bun add --dev` moves existing dependencies

`bun add -d`, `--optional` and `--peer` move a package that's already listed in another dependency group. They used to leave it where it was.

```sh
$ bun add -d typescript          # "dependencies" -> "devDependencies"
$ bun add --save-prod typescript # and back
```

### `bun install` reads the `.npmrc` that `actions/setup-node` writes

`actions/setup-node` writes its registry and token settings to a temporary `.npmrc` and points `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` at it. Bun reads that variable, so private registries work without copying the file.

```yaml#.github/workflows/ci.yml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    registry-url: https://npm.pkg.github.com
- run: bun install
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

### `bun install` understands npm, Yarn and pnpm flags, and rejects unknown ones

`bun install`, `bun ci`, `bun add`, `bun remove` and `bun update` translate flags from other package managers when Bun has an equivalent. Bun v1.4.3 ignored them, so `bun add --save-dev zod` saved to `dependencies` and `bun install --immutable` updated the lockfile.

| Flag                                                                        | Bun equivalent                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `--immutable`                                                               | `--frozen-lockfile`                        |
| `--package-lock-only`                                                       | `--lockfile-only`                          |
| `--save-dev`, `--save-exact`, `--save-optional`, `--save-peer`              | `--dev`, `--exact`, `--optional`, `--peer` |
| `--save-catalog`                                                            | `--catalog`                                |
| `--no-optional`, `--ignore-optional`                                        | `--omit=optional`                          |
| `--only=production`                                                         | `--omit=dev`                               |
| `--location=global`                                                         | `--global`                                 |
| `--shamefully-hoist`, `--node-linker=hoisted`, `--install-strategy=hoisted` | `--linker=hoisted`                         |
| `--node-linker=isolated`, `--install-strategy=linked`                       | `--linker=isolated`                        |

Flags with no Bun equivalent, like `--no-package-lock` or `--network-timeout 100000`, are ignored along with their value. Bun v1.4.3 only ignored the flag itself, so `bun install --network-timeout 100000` tried to add a package named `100000`.

Flags that none of these tools support are an error.

```sh
$ bun install --frozen-lockfil
error: bun install has no --frozen-lockfil flag.
note: Run 'bun install --help' for more information
```

Package manager commands and `bunx` used to ignore unknown flags, so this typo would silently run a normal install in CI.

### More in `bun install`

- `bun update --depth 0` only updates the dependencies in your `package.json`. Transitive dependencies keep the versions in `bun.lock`.
- `bun prune --check` prints what `bun prune` would remove without deleting anything, and exits with code 1 if there's anything to remove.
- `publishConfig.registry` and `publishConfig["@scope:registry"]` set the registry that `bun publish` publishes to.
- Like npm 11, `bun publish` refuses to publish a prerelease version like `2.0.0-beta.1` without `--tag` or `publishConfig.tag`, instead of tagging it `latest`.
- `workspace:*` can refer to the root package in `bun install`, `bun pm pack` and `bun publish`.
- `npm-shrinkwrap.json` is migrated, like `package-lock.json`.
- `bun.lock` records which packages have install scripts (`"hasInstallScript": true`), so installing from a committed lockfile reports blocked scripts. Older versions of Bun ignore the new key and drop it the next time they save the lockfile.
- When `bun install --frozen-lockfile` or `bun ci` fails because `package.json` changed, the error names the dependency, such as `is-odd was added` or `is-number changed from ^6.0.0 to ^7.0.0`.
- `--dry-run` works with `bun link`, `bun unlink`, `bun pm version`, `bun pm cache rm`, `bun pm trust`, `bun pm pkg` and `bun pm migrate`. Before, they accepted the flag but still wrote changes.
- `bun pm pkg set` and `delete` support arrays (`keywords[]=cli`, `contributors[0].name=Jane`) and bracketed keys (`exports[./package.json]`).
- `bun pm view` and `bun info` work outside of a project, accept multiple fields at once, and support npm-style paths like `maintainers[0].name`.
- `bun info`, `bun pm view`, `bun pm whoami` and `bun audit` retry failed requests like `bun install` does, instead of failing on a single 503 or dropped connection.
- `bun pm ls` accepts package names (`bun pm ls lodash`), `--production`, `--omit` and `--depth=0`.
- `bun pm version` sets `$npm_old_version`, `$npm_new_version`, `$npm_command` and `$npm_package_version` for the `preversion`, `version` and `postversion` scripts.
- Lifecycle scripts of dependencies get their own `npm_package_name`, `npm_package_version`, `npm_package_json` and `npm_package_config_*`, plus `npm_lifecycle_event`, `npm_lifecycle_script` and `npm_config_local_prefix`.
- `"gypfile": false` in a package disables the implicit `node-gyp rebuild`.
- `bun create <template>` supports `--ignore-scripts`. It also skips the template's preinstall and postinstall tasks when `ignoreScripts = true` is set in `bunfig.toml` or `ignore-scripts=true` in `.npmrc`.
- `bunx -p pkg cmd` installs `pkg`, then runs `cmd` with `pkg`'s binaries first in `PATH`, like npx.
- Auto-install reads registries and credentials from `.npmrc`.
- Auto-install uses the versions pinned in `bun.lock` or `bun.lockb`.
- Auto-install reads the project's `package.json` the same way `bun install` does: `devDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `overrides`, `resolutions` and `catalogs` are applied, and `workspace:`, `file:` and `link:` dependencies are loaded from disk.
- Security scanners receive every resolved dependency, including git, GitHub, tarball, `file:` and `link:` ones.
- `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `no-store` and a `max-age` under 5 minutes on registry metadata are respected.
- `--use-system-ca` works with `bun install` and the other package manager commands. Only `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` worked before.
- `BUN_INSTALL`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR`, `BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_DIR`, `BUN_INSTALL_BIN` and `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` accept a leading `~/`.
- `bun audit fix` reports and rewrites an `overrides` rule that pins a package to a vulnerable version.
- `bun pm migrate` on a Yarn v1 lockfile with 20,000 entries takes 0.27 s, down from 24 s.
- `bun install` in a monorepo with 2,100 workspaces peaks at 35 MB of memory, down from 91 MB.
- Applying a patch no longer takes quadratic time. `bun patch --commit` with 40,000 changed lines in a 100,000-line file takes 0.09 s instead of 1.45 s.
- With `globalStore = true`, a no-op `bun install` no longer deletes and re-creates every `node_modules/.bun/<pkg>` link. The store rebuilds its entries once after this upgrade, and `bun pm cache rm` frees the old ones.

Thanks to @nikelborm for the contribution!

## New in `Bun.SQL` and `bun:sqlite`

### `Bun.SQL` uses up to 48% less CPU per query

We reworked `Bun.SQL`, `bun:sqlite` and `node:sqlite` in a single change that replaces 149 open pull requests and fixes 51 issues.

Every query allocates less memory and executes fewer instructions on the client.

Client-side CPU usage with PostgreSQL, measured in user-space instructions on Linux x64:

| Operation                            | Change |
| ------------------------------------ | -----: |
| Point `SELECT`                       |   -48% |
| 100-row `SELECT`                     |   -30% |
| `INSERT`                             |   -21% |
| Bulk insert, 1,000 rows x 10 columns |   -38% |

The same bulk insert uses 53% fewer instructions on MySQL.

Garbage-collected objects allocated per `` await sql`select 1` ``:

| Adapter    | After | Before |
| ---------- | ----: | -----: |
| PostgreSQL |    28 |     84 |
| MySQL      |    27 |     76 |
| SQLite     |    33 |     52 |

### `query.cancel()` cancels a running PostgreSQL query

`cancel()` was already in the types and docs, but it didn't do anything. Now Bun asks the server to cancel the query, and the promise rejects with the server's error.

```ts
const query = sql`SELECT pg_sleep(30)`.execute();
setTimeout(() => query.cancel(), 100);

await query; // rejects: canceling statement due to user request
```

A query that hasn't been sent yet is never sent, and rejects with `ERR_POSTGRES_QUERY_CANCELLED`, `ERR_MYSQL_QUERY_CANCELLED` or `ERR_SQLITE_QUERY_CANCELLED`. On MySQL and MariaDB, a query that's already running on the server still runs to completion.

### `COPY` streams for PostgreSQL

`query.writable()` writes to `COPY ... FROM STDIN`, and `query.readable()` reads from `COPY ... TO STDOUT`. Both are web streams with backpressure, so memory usage stays flat no matter how large the table is.

```ts
// Load a CSV file into a table
await Bun.file("users.csv")
  .stream()
  .pipeTo(sql`COPY users (id, name) FROM STDIN (FORMAT csv)`.writable());

// Stream a table as an HTTP response
new Response(sql`COPY users TO STDOUT (FORMAT csv, HEADER)`.readable());
```

The streams carry raw bytes in whichever format the statement specifies: `text`, `csv` or `binary`. A 1,000 MiB `COPY` streams at 255 MiB/s with a peak RSS of 59 MiB.

Thanks to @gohryt for the contribution!

### Column name transforms in `Bun.SQL`

`transform: SQL.camel` converts column names in both directions: `first_name` is read as `firstName`, and `firstName` is written as `first_name`. It works with every adapter.

```ts
import { SQL } from "bun";

const sql = new SQL({ transform: SQL.camel });

await sql`INSERT INTO users ${sql({ firstName: "Alice" })}`;
// INSERT INTO users ("first_name") VALUES ($1)

const [user] = await sql`SELECT first_name FROM users`;
user.firstName; // "Alice"
```

- `SQL.camel`, `SQL.pascal` and `SQL.kebab` convert in both directions.
- `SQL.toCamel` only converts results, and `SQL.fromCamel` only converts names passed to `sql()` helpers. `pascal` and `kebab` have the same variants.
- `{ column: { from, to } }` accepts custom functions.

The names match postgres.js.

Thanks to @pjb3 for the contribution!

### Pass JavaScript arrays to PostgreSQL array columns

You can pass a JavaScript array or an `Int32Array` anywhere PostgreSQL expects a built-in array type, including arrays with `null`s and nested arrays. Both of these queries used to fail.

```ts
await sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ANY(${[1, 2, 3]})`;

// tags text[]
await sql`INSERT INTO posts ${sql({ title: "Hello", tags: ["bun", "sql"] })}`;
```

35 more built-in array types, such as `uuid[]`, `int4range[]` and `tsvector[]`, are returned as arrays instead of the string `"{...}"`.

For an array of a user-defined type such as an enum, use `sql.array(values, "mood")`.

### `result.columns` and `result.statement`

On PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, results include the column metadata reported by the server. Use `type` to distinguish columns that produce the same JavaScript value, such as `jsonb` and `text[]`.

```ts
const result = await sql`SELECT id, tags FROM posts WHERE id = ${1}`;

result.columns;
// [
//   { name: "id", type: 23, table: 16388, number: 1 }, // int4
//   { name: "tags", type: 1009, table: 16388, number: 2 }, // text[]
// ]

result.statement.string; // the text Bun sent, with $1 for the parameter
result.statement.types; // [23]
```

MySQL and MariaDB columns are `{ name, type, table, length, flags }`. Both properties are `null` on SQLite.

### `sql.json()`

`sql.json(value)` stores any value as JSON and works with every adapter. Use it for numbers, booleans, strings or `null`.

```ts
await sql`INSERT INTO settings (data) VALUES (${sql.json(42)})`; // 42
await sql`INSERT INTO settings (data) VALUES (${sql.json("dark")})`; // "dark"
await sql`INSERT INTO settings (data) VALUES (${sql.json(null)})`; // JSON null
```

A bare `null` is still SQL `NULL`.

### `bun --hot` reuses database connections

Every save under `bun --hot` used to open up to `max` new PostgreSQL or MySQL connections and leave the old ones open. Now a `new SQL()` with the same settings reuses the connections from before the reload.

With `max: 2`, five reloads used to leave 12 sessions open on the server. Now there are 2.

Session state like `SET` and temporary tables is preserved. `onconnect` runs again for each connection that's reused.

Thanks to @eriklangille for the contribution!

### New `Bun.SQL` connection options

```ts
const sql = new SQL("postgres://app@db.example.com/app?connect_timeout=5", {
  channelBinding: "require",
  tls: {
    ca: Bun.file("./ca.pem"),
    checkServerIdentity: (hostname, cert) =>
      cert.fingerprint256 === pin ? undefined : new Error("pin mismatch"),
  },
});
```

- `channelBinding`: `"disable"` (the default), `"prefer"` or `"require"`. It binds PostgreSQL SCRAM authentication to the server's TLS certificate (SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS). Also available as `?channel_binding=` and `PGCHANNELBINDING`.
- `tls.checkServerIdentity(hostname, cert)`: replaces the built-in hostname check on PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, like in `node:tls`. Passing it upgrades any SSL mode below `verify-ca` to `verify-full`.
- `foundRows: true`: on MySQL and MariaDB, `affectedRows` counts the rows an `UPDATE` matched instead of the rows it changed, like `mysql2`. Also available as `?foundRows=true`.
- `?connect_timeout=`, `?idle_timeout=`, `?max_lifetime=` and `?max=` in PostgreSQL and MySQL URLs.
- libpq's URL parameters on PostgreSQL: `host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `dbname`, `sslrootcert`, `sslcert`, `sslkey` and `sslpassword`. Bun used to forward them to the server, which refused the connection.
- `PGAPPNAME`, `PGOPTIONS` and `PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT` environment variables.

### User-defined functions in `bun:sqlite`

`db.function()` defines a SQL function that calls a JavaScript function.

```ts
import { Database } from "bun:sqlite";

const db = new Database(":memory:");
db.function("add2", (a, b) => a + b);

db.query("SELECT add2(12, 4) AS sum").get(); // { sum: 16 }
```

`db.aggregate()` defines an aggregate function such as `sum()`.

```ts
db.aggregate("add_all", {
  start: 0,
  step: (total, value) => total + value,
});

db.query("SELECT add_all(dollars) AS total FROM expenses").get();
```

- Both accept the `varargs`, `deterministic`, `directOnly` and `safeIntegers` options.
- `inverse` lets an aggregate be used as a window function.
- Errors thrown by a function propagate to the `get()`, `all()` or `run()` call that ran the query.

The signatures match better-sqlite3.

Thanks to @nikeee and @jdjkelly for the contribution!

### Update hooks in `bun:sqlite`

Set `db.onInsert`, `db.onUpdate` or `db.onDelete` to a function, and SQLite calls it for each row that this `Database` inserts, updates or deletes.

```ts
db.onInsert = (db, tableName, rowid) => {
  console.log(`inserted ${tableName} ${rowid}`);
};

db.run("INSERT INTO cats (name) VALUES ('Salem'), ('Keanu')");
// inserted cats 1
// inserted cats 2
```

Set it to `null` to remove the hook.

Also new:

- `stmt.reader` is `true` if the statement returns rows.
- `stmt.readonly` is `true` if the statement doesn't directly modify the database.
- `db[Symbol.for("sqlite-type")]` is `"bun:sqlite"`. Libraries can use it to distinguish a `Database` from a `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync`.

Thanks to @jecquas and @himself65 for the contribution!

## New in `WebSocket` and `ws`

### `ws` behaves like the npm package on Node.js

`import "ws"` in Bun loads a built-in implementation backed by Bun's native WebSocket client and server. We rewrote it as a port of `ws` 8.22.0. Framing, masking, UTF-8 validation and compression are still native.

| Compared to npm `ws` on Node.js                    | Bun v1.4.4 | Before |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ---------: | -----: |
| `ws`'s own test suite, 271 tests                   |        234 |     94 |
| 212 client scripts, byte-for-byte identical output |        179 |     18 |
| 159 server scripts, byte-for-byte identical output |        150 |     67 |

The remaining failures depend on `ws` internals that the native implementation doesn't have, like `ws._receiver` and `generateMask`.

```ts
import { WebSocket, createWebSocketStream } from "ws";

const ws = new WebSocket("wss://example.com/logs", {
  handshakeTimeout: 5_000,
  followRedirects: true,
  maxPayload: 1024 * 1024,
});

createWebSocketStream(ws, { encoding: "utf8" }).pipe(process.stdout);
```

- `createWebSocketStream()` is implemented, with backpressure. It used to throw "Not supported yet in Bun".
- `agent`, `createConnection` and `lookup` are respected, so SOCKS proxy agents work. A custom `agent` used to be ignored, and the client connected directly.
- `handshakeTimeout`, `closeTimeout`, `followRedirects`, `maxRedirects`, `origin`, `auth`, `protocolVersion`, `autoPong` and `skipUTF8Validation` are implemented instead of silently ignored.
- `maxPayload` is enforced on clients and servers. socket.io's `maxHttpBufferSize` depends on it.
- `WebSocketServer({ perMessageDeflate })` negotiates compression.
- `WebSocketServer` accepts any `Duplex`. This includes `http2.createSecureServer({ allowHTTP1: true })` (`vite --https`), `server.emit("connection", socket)` (socket.io sticky sessions) and fastify's `injectWS`.
- Server sockets have `pause()`, `resume()` and `isPaused`. They're `instanceof WebSocket`, and `ws._socket` is the `node:http` socket.

### `ws` events match Node.js

```ts
ws.on("error", (error) => {
  error instanceof Error; // true, was an ErrorEvent
  error.code; // "ECONNREFUSED"
});

ws.on("close", (code, reason) => {
  reason; // a Buffer, was a string
});
```

- An `'error'` event without a listener is an uncaught exception, like in Node.js. Add an `'error'` listener to every client and every server socket.
- `'close'` fires when the connection closes, with the peer's code and reason. `close()` without a code reports 1005, and a failed connection reports 1006.
- Error messages match the npm package's, like `Unexpected server response: 403`.
- `send()` throws while the socket is `CONNECTING`.
- `ws` servers have no idle timeout, no automatic pings and no backpressure limit. They used to inherit `Bun.serve`'s defaults: a 120 second idle timeout, a ping at 104 seconds and a 16 MiB limit.
- The default `maxPayload` is 100 MiB, up from 16 MiB.

### `WebSocket` waits for the closing handshake

The `close` event fires once the connection has closed, like in browsers and Node.js. It used to fire right after `close()` with your own code and `wasClean: true`, regardless of what the server did.

```ts
const ws = new WebSocket("wss://example.com");
ws.onopen = () => ws.close();

ws.onclose = (event) => {
  event.code; // the server's code, 1005 if its Close frame had none
  event.wasClean; // false if the server never sent a Close frame
};
```

- `close()` without a code sends an empty Close frame. Both ends report 1005 instead of 1000, including the `close(ws, code)` handler in `Bun.serve`.
- A script that ends with `ws.close()` takes one extra round trip to exit. If the server doesn't respond within 30 seconds, `close` fires with 1006.
- `BUN_CONFIG_WS_CLOSE_TIMEOUT` changes the 30 second timeout. `ws.terminate()` closes immediately.

### Failed `WebSocket` connections fire `error`, then `close` with 1006

A bad handshake, a TLS or proxy error, a protocol error, an oversized message and invalid UTF-8 are all reported the same way, like in browsers and Node.js. `event.error.code` is new.

```ts
const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:1");

ws.onerror = (event) => {
  event.error.code; // "ECONNREFUSED"
};

ws.onclose = (event) => {
  event.code; // 1006
  event.reason; // ""
  event.wasClean; // false
};
```

Before, `close` fired with 1002, 1007, 1009, 1011 or 1015 and an English reason, sometimes with `wasClean: true`, and often no `error` event fired.

- `event.message` has the description that used to be in `reason`, with more detail: `Expected 101 status code: 503`, `TLS handshake failed: self signed certificate`.
- `event.error.code` is a Node.js-style code such as `ENOTFOUND`, `DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT`, `ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID` or `WS_ERR_INVALID_UTF8`.
- Losing the TCP connection after `open` isn't treated as a failure. Only `close` fires, with 1006.

### `ws.pause()` and `ws.resume()` in `Bun.serve`

Use these to slow down a client that sends faster than you can process. While a socket is paused, Bun stops reading from it, so the client sees TCP backpressure.

```ts
Bun.serve({
  fetch(req, server) {}, // upgrade logic
  websocket: {
    message(ws, message) {
      if (!file.write(message)) {
        ws.pause();
        file.once("drain", () => ws.resume());
      }
    },
  },
});
```

`ws.isPaused` tells you whether the socket is paused. The idle timeout is suspended while a socket is paused.

### `websocket.error` in `Bun.serve` receives the socket

When a `websocket` handler throws, Bun calls `error` with the error and the socket it came from. It only received the error before, and it was missing from the types.

```ts
Bun.serve({
  fetch(req, server) {}, // upgrade logic
  websocket: {
    message(ws, message) {
      throw new Error("oops");
    },
    error(error, ws) {
      ws.close(1011);
    },
  },
});
```

Every handler is optional, including `message`.

### `proxy.tls`: separate TLS options for an HTTPS proxy

With an `https://` proxy, `tls` applies to both the proxy and the server. Pass `proxy.tls` to configure them separately. The proxy then only uses `proxy.tls`, and the server only uses `tls`.

```ts
const ws = new WebSocket("wss://example.com", {
  proxy: {
    url: "https://proxy.internal:8443",
    tls: { ca: Bun.file("./proxy-ca.pem") },
  },
});
```

Thanks to @steipete, @hughescr, @davidhevn and @deepshekhardas for the contributions!

## New in the runtime

### JavaScriptCore upgrade

This release upgrades JavaScriptCore with 1,013 upstream WebKit commits.

Measured on an Apple silicon Mac, best of several runs:

| Operation                                                       | Bun v1.4.4 | Bun v1.4.3 | Faster |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------: | ---------: | -----: |
| `n.toLocaleString("en-US")`, 100,000 calls                      |      25 ms |   1,341 ms |    54x |
| Loading an array literal of 1,000,000 integers                  |      11 ms |      45 ms |   4.2x |
| `for (const ch of str)`, 1,000,000 characters, some non-Latin-1 |     1.2 ms |     3.2 ms |   2.7x |
| `new Array(n)` with `n` under 4, 10,000,000 calls               |      31 ms |      61 ms |   2.0x |
| `try { throw "x" } catch {}`, 1,000,000 times                   |      37 ms |      72 ms |   2.0x |
| `try { throw new Error("x") } catch {}`, 1,000,000 times        |     128 ms |     174 ms |   1.4x |
| `new WeakMap()` and one `set()`, 1,000,000 times                |     7.7 ms |     9.9 ms |   1.3x |

`toLocaleString()` with a locale and no options reuses a cached `Intl.NumberFormat`, which makes it as fast as creating the formatter yourself and calling `format()`. This applies to numbers and BigInts.

- `using` is allowed in a function nested inside a `switch` case. It was a `SyntaxError`.
- `+1n * 2n` throws a `TypeError`. It used to return `2n`.
- `+a * b()` calls `a.valueOf()` before `b()`.
- `for...in` over a function visits its indexed properties, like `fn[0]`.
- JIT-optimized `(x + y + 0.5) | 0` returns the right result when `x + y` overflows 32 bits.
- JIT-optimized code throws a `RangeError` for `new Uint8Array(-1)` even if the array is never used.
- In sloppy mode, `label: function f() {}` is hoisted like an unlabeled function declaration.
- WebAssembly's baseline compiler keeps a function's most-used locals in registers.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/f2405c382d43b89d91a2e7c90d9c5f53505a1e71 -->

### `Bun.Glob` supports extglob and brace ranges

```ts
const source = new Bun.Glob("**/!(*.test).ts");
source.match("src/cart.ts"); // true
source.match("src/cart.test.ts"); // false

new Bun.Glob("src/@(app|lib)/**/*.ts").match("src/app/a/b.ts"); // true
new Bun.Glob("shard-{1..3}.json").match("shard-2.json"); // true
```

| Pattern                                     | Matches                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `?(a\|b)`                                   | Zero or one of the patterns                                   |
| `*(a\|b)`                                   | Zero or more of the patterns                                  |
| `+(a\|b)`                                   | One or more of the patterns                                   |
| `@(a\|b)`                                   | Exactly one of the patterns                                   |
| `!(a\|b)`                                   | Anything in a path segment except the patterns                |
| `{1..3}`, `{01..10}`, `{a..e}`, `{1..9..2}` | A number or letter in the range. The third value is the step. |

The new syntax works everywhere Bun uses globs, including `--filter` and `workspaces`, `files` and `sideEffects` in `package.json`.

```json#package.json
{
  "workspaces": ["packages/!(internal)"]
}
```

In Bun v1.4.3, this failed with `error: Workspace not found "packages/!(internal)"`.

A `(` that isn't preceded by `?`, `*`, `+`, `@` or `!` is still a literal character, so Next.js route groups like `app/(marketing)/**` still match.

These patterns used to be matched literally. They now have a different meaning, consistent with picomatch, minimatch and bash's `extglob`:

| Pattern     | Bun v1.4.3                | Bun v1.4.4                                                 |
| ----------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `*(1).txt`  | Matched `copy(1).txt`     | Zero or more `1`, then `.txt`. Write `*[(]1).txt` instead. |
| `!(g)/a.ts` | Everything but `(g)/a.ts` | `a.ts` in any folder but `g`                               |
| `{1..3}`    | The text `1..3`           | `1`, `2` or `3`                                            |

This only affects patterns, not paths. A file with those characters in its name still matches `**/*.ts`.

Bun Shell is unaffected: quoted text and `${}` values are still treated literally.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/bfa1209e35663056248406661f1b90851e5c72fa -->

### Up to 2.8x faster `Headers` iteration

`for...of`, `entries()`, `keys()`, `values()`, `forEach()` and `Object.fromEntries(headers)` are 1.7x to 2.8x faster. Adapters that copy a `Response`'s headers into `node:http`, like `@hono/node-server`, do this on every request.

```ts
for (const [name, value] of response.headers) {
  res.setHeader(name, value);
}
```

Time to iterate over one `Headers` object on an M4 Max, best of 7 runs:

| Operation                                 |  v1.4.4 |  v1.4.3 | Faster |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------: | ------: | -----: |
| `for...of`, 3 headers                     |   98 ns |  277 ns |   2.8x |
| `for...of`, 14 headers                    |  627 ns | 1.41 µs |   2.2x |
| `for...of`, 14 custom `X-` headers        | 1.24 µs | 2.08 µs |   1.7x |
| `headers.forEach()`, 14 headers           |  505 ns | 1.10 µs |   2.2x |
| `[...headers.keys()]`, 14 headers         |  261 ns |  688 ns |   2.6x |
| `[...headers.values()]`, 14 headers       |  295 ns |  680 ns |   2.3x |
| `Object.fromEntries(headers)`, 14 headers |  579 ns | 1.46 µs |   2.5x |

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/408c9374b266b45fe6b8260e09be73aa82a957cd -->

### Up to 2.6x faster `response.body` streams for in-memory bodies

Streaming a body that's already in memory (`new Response("...").body`, `request.body`, `blob.stream()`) is 1.5x to 2.6x faster. Reading a 100-byte body allocates 7 KB instead of 270 KB.

```ts
for await (const chunk of new Response(html).body) {
  res.write(chunk);
}
```

Time to read an entire `new Response(string).body` with `reader.read()`, on Linux x64:

| Body  |   After |   Before |
| ----- | ------: | -------: |
| 100 B | 1.41 µs |  3.66 µs |
| 4 KB  | 1.77 µs |  4.15 µs |
| 16 KB | 2.93 µs |  5.54 µs |
| 64 KB | 9.11 µs | 14.33 µs |
| 1 MB  |  176 µs |   272 µs |

Adapters that copy a `Response` into a `node:http` response read the body this way. A Hono app on `@hono/node-server` handled a batch of 24 requests in 16.0 ms, down from 24.0 ms.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/5ee74f02a2586059ab4d496a0f35d3a788e5e807 -->

### `--disallow-code-generation-from-strings=strict` only runs code that ships with your program

`=strict` used to block a fixed list of APIs. Now JavaScriptCore refuses to run any code that isn't a Bun built-in or one of your program's own files, regardless of which API it came from.

For a `bun build --compile` executable, only the code inside the executable counts as your program. JavaScript and TypeScript files on disk no longer run, including files the program just wrote:

```ts
const path = "/tmp/plugin.js";
await Bun.write(path, "console.log('hi')");
await import(path);
// EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context
```

Without `--compile`, files on disk count as your program, so that import still runs.

`=strict` also blocks:

- Plugins that return `contents`, for any loader. Return an `exports` object instead.
- Macros.
- In a compiled executable, `--preload` in `BUN_OPTIONS` and `.txt` or `.md` imports from disk.

`.json`, `.toml` and `.yaml` files still load from disk. `import()` of a `data:` URL containing JSON is no longer blocked.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/5f5799ed16568240de19fef364bd4c9bf22ca1c7 -->

## New in the dev server

### Redesigned error overlay in the dev server

The error overlay for `Bun.serve` with HTML imports has a new design, and similar errors in the same file are grouped into one card. Three missing fonts in a stylesheet used to show up as three separate blocks.

```txt
BUILD FAILED
4 errors in 2 files

app.ts                                         1 ERROR
  ERROR  Could not resolve: "./render"
      1  import { render } from "./render";

styles.css                                    3 ERRORS
  ERROR  Could not resolve                          ×3
      3  src: url("./fonts/inter-regular.woff2");
      8  src: url("./fonts/inter-medium.woff2");
     13  src: url("./fonts/inter-bold.woff2");
```

- The overlay scrolls. Errors past the bottom of the window used to be unreachable.
- Build errors are shown once, not twice, when a file is bundled for both the server and the browser, like a stylesheet imported by a page.
- There's a light theme that follows your system setting.
- Runtime errors use the same design, with the error's name as the title.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/91e7e3b140eaef348b7bc33d564dcb67b7de4ddd -->

## Other improvements

- Improved: `req.headers` and `res.setHeader()` have less overhead in `node:http` servers. 256 requests through Express 5 take 9.45 ms, down from 9.91 ms (Linux x64).

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/61009bd2f332822cbf29e69829bbe9c33e3c2150 -->

- Improved: `Bun.JSON5.parse()` is up to 1.6x faster. A 126 KB `bun.lock` parses in 0.42 ms, down from 0.67 ms (M4 Max).

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/788087c0a4e0c4e57dfe78156ba57a70e329d1b1 -->

- Improved: `Bun.Glob.match()` is 1.6x to 5x faster. Matching `**/*.{ts,tsx}` against `src/components/button/index.tsx` takes 32 ns, down from 158 ns (M4 Max).

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/bfa1209e35663056248406661f1b90851e5c72fa -->

- Improved: root certificates are updated to NSS 3.131.1.

- Improved: native addons on Linux and macOS can call 47 more libuv functions, including `uv_async_*`, `uv_timer_*`, `uv_idle_*`, `uv_prepare_*`, `uv_check_*`, `uv_queue_work`, `uv_default_loop` and `uv_cwd`. Bun used to exit with "unsupported uv function".
- Improved: echoing a 1 MB non-ASCII WebSocket text message in `Bun.serve` takes 72% fewer CPU instructions.
- Improved: `Bun.markdown.html()` on large non-ASCII input takes 33% fewer CPU instructions.

- Improved: `Bun.hash()` and its algorithms are 1.2x to 2.3x faster on short strings. `Bun.hash.crc32()` on a 16-character ASCII string takes 8 ns, down from 15 ns (M4 Max).
- Improved: `Bun.CryptoHasher`, `Bun.SHA256` and the other hashers are 1.2x to 1.7x faster on small inputs. Hashing 16 bytes to hex with `Bun.SHA256.hash()` takes 77 ns, down from 107 ns (M4 Max).

- Improved: `new TextDecoder()` with an options object, like `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })`, is 2x faster.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/3880151f0abacaf7dce9d6d0ab1c7be295d14bb4 -->

- Fixed: a regression in Bun v1.4.3 where runs that write the compile cache (`NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` or `module.enableCompileCache()`) took 2x longer to exit (580 ms instead of 300 ms for a 3.4 MB module).

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/0663016fd8e3f824b1ecf6298ca6b4595d40f8d4 -->

- Improved: Bun's FreeBSD binaries are built against FreeBSD 14.4. The previous target, 14.3, has reached end of life.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/b7efd52c3b36c17a29e7485fd8a45962ac2af701 -->

## Security

This release includes security fixes for TLS, WebSocket, the database clients and the package manager. These protocols, APIs and commands are affected:

TLS, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, WebSocket, Brotli, `Bun.serve`, `Bun.listen`, `Bun.connect`, `Bun.SQL`, `Bun.RedisClient`, `Bun.password`, `Bun.Image`, `Bun.Archive`, `node:tls`, `node:https`, `node:http`, `node:http2`, `node:net`, `node:quic`, `node:crypto`, `node:vm`, `node:v8`, `ws`, `fetch`, `TextEncoder`, `bun install`, `bunx`, `bun patch`, `bun publish`, `bun pm pack`, `bun pm trust`, `bun audit` and `bun create`.

## Bugfixes

### Node.js compatibility improvements

- Fixed: various stability issues in `node:http`, `node:http2`, `node:quic`, `node:dgram`, `node:dns`, `node:crypto`, `node:vm`, `node:stream`, `node:zlib`, `node:util`, `node:diagnostics_channel`, `node:worker_threads` and native addons.

#### `node:http`

- Fixed: in a `node:http` server, `res.end()` threw `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` when `res.statusCode` was a numeric string like `"404"` or a fraction like `200.5`. It now sends `404` and `200`, like Node.js.
- Fixed: in a `node:http` server, `res.end()` sent `200` when `res.statusCode` was `NaN` or `undefined`. It now throws `ERR_HTTP_INVALID_STATUS_CODE`, like Node.js.
- Fixed: in a `node:http` server, after `res.end({})` threw because of the invalid chunk, `res.headersSent` was `true` even though nothing had been sent, so `res.setHeader()` threw `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/59c1ac474cdbafe9d77b395bd2712b767b617767 -->

#### `node:http2`

- Fixed: `pushStream()` in `node:http2` threw `ERR_HTTP2_OUT_OF_STREAMS` instead of passing it to the callback.
- Fixed: with `http2.createSecureServer()` and `server.emit("connection", socket)`, `session.socket` wasn't a `TLSSocket` and `'connection'` listeners didn't fire.

#### `node:fs`

- Fixed: on Linux and macOS, every `fs.realpath()` variant treated `\` as a path separator, so a file named `a\b` threw `ENOENT`, or resolved to `a/b` if that existed.
- Fixed: on Linux and macOS, `fs.realpath.native()`, `fs.realpathSync.native()` and `fs.promises.realpath()` collapsed `..` before following symlinks, so `link/../y` resolved next to the link instead of its target, and `missing/..` didn't throw.
- Fixed: on Linux and macOS, `fs.realpath()` and `fs.realpathSync()` threw `ENOTDIR` for a regular file's path with a trailing slash, like `file/`. Like Node.js, they now return the file's path.
- Fixed: on Windows, `fs.promises.realpath("C:\\")` returned `C:` instead of `C:\`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/c0e1716f17386fb1683320ea1c7ac78c33c48a3a -->

#### `node:vm`

- Fixed: `vm.createContext(vm.constants.DONT_CONTEXTIFY)` returned a wrapper instead of the context's global. Top-level `var` and `function` declarations were lost, and Vitest with jsdom 30.1 failed to start.
- Fixed: in a `vm.createContext(vm.constants.DONT_CONTEXTIFY)` context, scripts threw a `ReferenceError` for names inherited from the global's prototype chain, including through a `Proxy`. jsdom 30 with `runScripts` relies on this.

#### `node:stream`

- Fixed: `Readable.fromWeb(stream).destroy()` emitted `'error'` when the web stream's `cancel()` rejected. Node.js doesn't.

#### `node:crypto`

- Fixed: an X25519 `CryptoKey` couldn't be cloned with `structuredClone()` or sent with `postMessage()`.
- Fixed: `write()` on a `node:crypto` `Hash` or `Hmac` threw `ERR_CRYPTO_HASH_FINALIZED` after `digest()`. The chunk is now dropped, like in Node.js.

#### `node:util`

- Fixed: calling `new` on a native function that isn't a constructor, like `util.types.isDate`, returned the result of calling it. It now throws a `TypeError`, like Node.js. These functions were also printed as `[class isDate]`.
- Fixed: `util.types.isProxy(globalThis)` returned `true`.

#### `process`

- Fixed: registering the same function twice with `process.on()` only added it once. It's now added and called twice, like in Node.js.
- Fixed: after `import * as process from "node:process"`, `process.on()` didn't add the listener to `process`.

#### `node:diagnostics_channel`

- Fixed: in `node:diagnostics_channel`, the next subscriber was skipped when a subscriber unsubscribed itself during `publish()`.
- Fixed: in `node:diagnostics_channel`, a subscriber added during `publish()` was called during that same `publish()`.
- Fixed: `channel.unsubscribe()` threw a `TypeError` when `channel._subscribers` held a frozen or sealed array.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/a407eae88ac76d2f54068b00a9f79c7b9ccc0f0f -->

#### `node:worker_threads`

- Fixed: in a `Worker` with `env: SHARE_ENV`, `join()`, `slice()` and `concat()` treated holes as empty in an array with `process.env` in its prototype chain. `arr[1]` already read `process.env[1]`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/dbe1a63c86436c79652b24f919e7d3393a82d411 -->

#### Native addons

- Fixed: loading a `NODE_MODULE` addon in a Worker when the main thread has already loaded it now throws `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`, like Node.js.
- Fixed: when a Worker stopped while a native addon's async work was still running, the addon's finalizers ran before that work was done. They now run after it, like in Node.js.

#### Other modules

- Fixed: the `write()` callback on a `node:net` or `node:tls` socket was never called if the connection closed while the write was still pending. It's now called with `ECANCELED`, like in Node.js.

- Fixed: `os.userInfo()` threw `TypeError: Type error` when passed a number or a string. It now behaves like Node.js.
- Fixed: `os.setPriority(priority, undefined)` threw. It now behaves like Node.js.

- Fixed: `socket.connect()` in `node:dgram` failed with `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` when the port was a numeric string like `"41234"`. Node.js accepts it.
- Fixed: `zlib.crc32(data, undefined)` threw `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`. It now starts from `0`, like `zlib.crc32(data)`.
- Fixed: `http.maxHeaderSize = "5000000000"` wrapped to `705032704`. The setter now only accepts a safe integer of 1 or more, and a string like `"16384"` throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/ed58ba2126e84127dbb64c29cbddc103a67f77b1 -->

- Fixed: `new SourceMap()` from `node:module` threw `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` when `mappings` was an empty string, like in the source map of a chunk that only re-exports.
- Fixed: `Profiler.takePreciseCoverage` in `node:inspector` returned function and block ranges that didn't match V8's, so tools like `v8-to-istanbul` marked the wrong lines. A skipped `?? fallback()` was counted as executed.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/6f58f6b89446918c534223c3c32df7feec62abea -->

### Bun APIs

- Fixed: various stability issues in `Bun.serve`, `Bun.spawn`, `FileSink`, `Bun.S3Client`, `Bun.RedisClient`, `Bun.YAML`, `Bun.JSON5`, `Bun.markdown`, `Bun.Cookie`, `Bun.WebView`, `HTMLRewriter`, `bun:ffi`, `Bun.gzipSync()`, `Bun.deflateSync()` and `Bun.unsafe.arrayBufferToString()`.

#### `Bun.serve`

- Fixed: an error thrown by a `Bun.serve` request handler in a Worker is now printed, like on the main thread.

#### `Bun.hash` and `Bun.CryptoHasher`

- Fixed: `Bun.hash()` and its algorithms returned the hash of an empty input when given a `Bun.file()`, an S3 file or a `Bun.build()` output written to `outdir`. They now throw a `TypeError`.
- Fixed: hashing an S3 file with `Bun.CryptoHasher`, `Bun.SHA1.hash()`, `Bun.sha()` or `crypto.hash()` returned the digest of an empty input. It now throws a `TypeError`, like it does for `Bun.file()`.
- Fixed: `Bun.hash()`, `Bun.hash(undefined)` and `Bun.hash(null)` returned the hash of `""`, `"undefined"` and `"null"`. They now throw a `TypeError`, and so do `Bun.hash.crc32()` and the other algorithms.
- Fixed: accessing the static `byteLength` on a subclass of `Bun.MD5`, `Bun.SHA256` or another hasher threw a `TypeError`, and so did `algorithms` on a subclass of `Bun.CryptoHasher`.

#### `Bun.Glob`

- Fixed: `Bun.Glob.match()` treated `**` inside braces like `*`, so `{src/**,lib/**}` didn't match `src/a/b.ts`.
- Fixed: `Bun.Glob.match()` returned `false` for a pattern with more than 10 brace groups, or with braces nested more than 10 deep.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/bfa1209e35663056248406661f1b90851e5c72fa -->

- Fixed: `Bun.Glob`'s `scan()` and `scanSync()` treated a truthy option that isn't `true` as `false`. `{ dot: 1 }` skipped dotfiles and `{ onlyFiles: 1 }` listed directories.

#### Other Bun APIs

- Fixed: `Bun.JSON5.parse()` accepted two invalid inputs. `"1\0 2"` parsed as `1` and `"{a\\u002d: 1}"` as `{ a: 1 }`. Both throw a `SyntaxError`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/788087c0a4e0c4e57dfe78156ba57a70e329d1b1 -->

- Fixed: `Bun.markdown.ansi()` and `bun file.md` could break a line in the middle of a word made of several parts, like `` `code` `` followed by `.` or `(` followed by a link.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/bfa1209e35663056248406661f1b90851e5c72fa -->

- Fixed: `.ptr` on a `bun:ffi` `cc()` symbol wasn't the address of the C function.

- Fixed: `Bun.YAML.parse()` returned `null` and `Bun.TOML.parse()` returned `{}` when given an S3 file. They now throw a `TypeError`, like they do for `Bun.file()`.

- Fixed: `Bun.gzipSync()` and `Bun.deflateSync()` ignored the `memLevel` and `strategy` options and always compressed with the defaults. A `memLevel` outside 1 to 9 or a `strategy` outside 0 to 4 now throws.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/d0831bc9fe53ceec29281fb9b7dfdebea39bc351 -->

- Fixed: `Bun.CSRF.generate(undefined, options)` threw "Secret is required", so there was no way to pass options and keep the default secret.
- Fixed: `Bun.$.escape()` returned non-string arguments like `null`, `true` or `new String("foo")` unchanged when they didn't need escaping. It now always returns a string.
- Improved: `expiresIn: NaN` in `Bun.CSRF.generate()`, `maxAge: NaN` in `Bun.CSRF.verify()` and a `NaN` port in `Bun.dns.prefetch()` throw a `RangeError` instead of falling back to the default.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/21620e2be3959ed985d971c60565a98a142e4503 -->

- Fixed: `Bun.indexOfLine()` returned `-1` when its first argument wasn't a buffer, such as a string that contains a newline. It now throws a `TypeError`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/0a2f1c815699d8fd7ab5a7db52493d8e79e34109 -->

- Fixed: `Bun.JSONL.parseChunk()` reported a `read` offset before a value it had already returned when that value was followed by a stray `,`, `]` or `}`. Regression in v1.4.3.
- Fixed: `Bun.JSONL.parse()` and `Bun.JSONL.parseChunk()` returned a value more than once when it was preceded by blank lines and followed by a stray `,`, `]` or `}`. Regression in v1.4.3.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/281698ac9380110414b293017531b39466014ad3 -->

- Fixed: `assetPrefix` on a `Bun.FileSystemRouter` was always `undefined`. It now returns the `assetPrefix` option, or `null` if it isn't set.
- Fixed: `query` and `params` from `Bun.FileSystemRouter`'s `match()` listed numeric keys twice, so `Object.values(router.match("/?0=a").query)` returned `["a", "a"]`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/3880151f0abacaf7dce9d6d0ab1c7be295d14bb4 -->

- Fixed: `graph.dispose()` on a `Bun.ModuleGraph` leaked the graph's modules when its code still had a `Bun.Terminal` open or a `node:http` server listening. The terminal's file descriptors leaked too.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/392cf216453ac44be360c7fafdffdf509d3c428c -->

### Web APIs

- Fixed: various stability issues in experimental HTTP/2 `fetch()`, `ReadableStream.from()`, `crypto.subtle`, `structuredClone`, `URL`, `URLSearchParams`, `URLPattern`, `Headers` and `FormData`.

#### `fetch`

- Fixed: `fetch()` with `keepalive: false`, or a `keepAlive: false` `Bun.FetchSession`, left its HTTP/1.1 connection open in the pool when the request also had a `Connection: keep-alive` header, which happens when you forward `req.headers`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/6fbfdcd7efee8cfe8101e5f7afbbcda5d5c0f95e -->

#### Streams and `Blob`

- Fixed: `new Response(blob, { headers }).blob()` set `type` on the original `Blob` when it had none.
- Fixed: `slice()` without a type on a body `Blob` kept the parent's type instead of `""`.

#### Other Web APIs

- Fixed: `Reflect.construct()` of `WebSocket`, `BroadcastChannel` or `Worker` still connected, subscribed or started the thread when the `newTarget`'s `prototype` getter threw.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/39bbb7182cf9eb31a3328195b4198012946f8b9a -->

### TLS

- Fixed: various stability issues in TLS clients and servers.

- Improved: `Bun.serve`, `Bun.listen` and `node:tls` servers now only request a client certificate when `requestCert: true` is set, which matches the docs and Node.js. Setting `ca` alone no longer does. For mTLS, set both.
- Fixed: a `tls.createServer()` with `SNICallback` never negotiated ALPN. `ALPNProtocols` and `ALPNCallback` were ignored, so HTTP/2 clients fell back to HTTP/1.1.
- Fixed: the `ws` package ignored top-level TLS options such as `rejectUnauthorized`, `ca`, `cert` and `key`, so connecting to a self-signed `wss://` server failed with `TLS handshake failed`. `pfx` is also supported.
- Fixed: `node-fetch` ignored the TLS options (`ca`, `cert`, `key`, `rejectUnauthorized`) of an `https.Agent` passed as `agent`.
- Fixed: `fetch()`, `tls.connect()` and other TLS clients failed to connect to servers with an Ed25519 certificate.
- Fixed: a self-signed certificate that isn't marked as a CA, like the ones `dotnet dev-certs` creates, wasn't trusted when passed in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or `ca`.
- Fixed: a TLS server configured with multiple `key` and `cert` pairs only served the last one. With an RSA and an ECDSA pair, each client now gets one it supports.
- Fixed: assigning `tls.DEFAULT_CIPHERS` had no effect on `fetch`, `WebSocket`, `Bun.connect`, `RedisClient`, `Bun.SQL` and `S3Client`.
- Fixed: `Bun.SQL` with `sslmode=prefer` timed out against a Postgres server without TLS. It now falls back to an unencrypted connection, as documented.
- Fixed: `Bun.SQL` ignored `tls.servername`, the `node:tls` spelling of `serverName`.
- Fixed: `tls.connect()` with `autoSelectFamily` added an `'end'` listener for each address it tried, and printed `MaxListenersExceededWarning` after nine.

- Fixed: the `tls` options `key`, `cert`, `ca`, `crl` and `ALPNProtocols` read the entire underlying `ArrayBuffer` when given a view into part of it, like `buffer.subarray(n)`.

### WebSocket

- Fixed: various stability issues in the `WebSocket` client and `ws`.

#### `WebSocket` client

- Fixed: a client `WebSocket`'s `send()`, `ping()` and `pong()` sent the text `[object BuildArtifact]` when given an in-memory `Bun.build()` output. They now send its bytes, like `ServerWebSocket`.

- Fixed: `ws.send()` right before `ws.close()` could lose messages on `ws://` if the server was still sending, while `close` reported a clean 1000.
- Fixed: on `wss://` through a proxy, Close and Pong frames could be sent ahead of queued messages, which were then lost even though the close was reported as clean.
- Fixed: a `wss://` `WebSocket` connected through a proxy closed with 1006 when a frame was sent while a TLS 1.2 server was renegotiating. Direct connections weren't affected.
- Fixed: in rare cases under backpressure, the end of the send queue was never flushed and `bufferedAmount` stayed above 0.
- Fixed: event listeners didn't run in the `AsyncLocalStorage` context of the `new WebSocket()` call.
- Fixed: `new WebSocket(url, { protocols: "chat" })` threw "Value is not a sequence", and `protocol: "chat"` was ignored.
- Fixed: `ws://:token@host` sent no credentials.
- Fixed: one invalid entry in `proxy.headers` silently dropped all of them, including `Proxy-Authorization`. It now throws instead.
- Fixed: a proxy's 407 was reported as "Proxy connection failed", and a CONNECT reply of `HTTP/1.1 200` with no reason phrase, or any 2xx other than 200, was rejected.
- Fixed: `100 Continue` or `103 Early Hints` before the 101 failed the handshake.
- Fixed: `send()`, `ping()` and `pong()` with `Bun.file()` or an S3 file sent an empty frame. They now throw.
- Fixed: non-ASCII header values were sent as UTF-8. They're now sent as Latin-1, like `fetch` and Node.js.
- Fixed: several `WebSocket` TypeScript types. `error` and `onerror` receive an `ErrorEvent`, the `ping` and `pong` events and `binaryType: "blob"` are declared, and `headers` accepts a `Headers` object.

#### `Bun.serve` WebSocket servers

- Fixed: Safari closed the connection with 1002 when a server with `perMessageDeflate: true` sent compressed messages.
- Fixed: `perMessageDeflate.compress` set to `"dedicated"` or `"4KB"` through `"256KB"` was treated as `"3KB"`. Each value now uses its own window size, which uses more memory: `"dedicated"` goes from 149 KB to 282 KB per connection.
- Fixed: `perMessageDeflate: { compress: false, decompress: true }` still compressed outgoing messages, and `decompress: "16KB"` configured the compressor.
- Fixed: `server.stop(true)` closed WebSockets with 1006. They now close with 1001 "Server closed".
- Fixed: after a protocol error, invalid UTF-8 or a message over `maxPayloadLength`, the client saw 1006. It now receives a Close frame with 1002, 1007 or 1009 and a reason.
- Fixed: `idleTimeout: 0` closed idle connections after about 256 seconds instead of never.
- Fixed: `idleTimeout: 65536`, `maxPayloadLength: 2 ** 32 + 16` and `backpressureLimit: 2 ** 32 + 1` wrapped around to 0, 16 and 1.
- Fixed: `maxPayloadLength` also applied to Ping, Pong and Close frames.
- Fixed: `ws.close()` on a socket over `backpressureLimit` dropped messages that `send()` had already accepted, along with the Close frame.
- Fixed: `ws.close()` inside `ws.cork()`, `drain`, or `open` after an async upgrade closed the connection 16 seconds late.
- Fixed: `terminate()`, a throwing `open` handler, `stop(true)` and process exit dropped data that `send()` or `publish()` had accepted in the same tick.
- Fixed: a long `ws.close(code, reason)` reason was truncated in the middle of a character, so the client saw 1007.
- Fixed: `server.upgrade(req, { headers })` sent `Sec-WebSocket-Accept`, `Upgrade` or `Connection` twice when `headers` had them, threw for `headers: {}`, and couldn't decline a subprotocol. An empty `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` now declines it.
- Fixed: an error thrown after `server.upgrade()` was silently dropped. It's now passed to `error()` or printed to stderr.
- Fixed: `server.reload()` leaked memory for every route of a server with WebSockets, and new `websocket` options didn't apply to sockets that were already open.

#### `ws`

- Fixed: a `ws` server sending a burst of large messages delivered some twice and some out of order.
- Fixed: `ws.once("message")` together with `ws.on("message")` delivered each message twice.
- Fixed: on server sockets, `addEventListener("message")` received a `Buffer` for text, and `onclose` received a number.
- Fixed: the `binary` option of `send()` was ignored for an `ArrayBuffer` or `Blob`, and `{ fin: false }` sent whole messages instead of fragments.
- Fixed: the `send()` callback reported success for a message dropped after `close()`. Callbacks now run once the data is written, or with an error if the socket closes first.
- Fixed: the `send()`, `ping()` and `pong()` callbacks reported success for a frame dropped after the connection ended but before `'close'` fired. They now receive `ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED`, like in Node.js.
- Fixed: messages that arrived before a deferred `handleUpgrade()`, after an `await` or an async `verifyClient`, were lost.
- Fixed: in `'unexpected-response'`, a chunked body arrived undecoded, and a body that came after the response head was lost.
- Fixed: `ws` ignored `proxyRequestOptions.headers` of an `hpagent` proxy agent, so proxies that require `Proxy-Authorization` responded with 407.
- Fixed: headers pushed by a `'headers'` listener were missing from the 101 response (engine.io's cookies), and `handleProtocols: () => false` still selected a protocol (graphql-ws).

#### `node:http` and `undici`
