- Fixed: `socket.bytesWritten` was 0 on `'upgrade'` and `'connect'` sockets in `node:http`. engine.io closes such sockets after a second, so a Vite or SvelteKit dev server with socket.io reloaded the page every second.
- Fixed: Slack Bolt in Socket Mode reconnected forever, because `undici` had no `ping()` export and no `undici:websocket:ping` and `undici:websocket:pong` diagnostics channels.

### Runtime

- Fixed: various stability issues in startup on Linux arm64, garbage collection on Linux and uncaught error reporting.

- Fixed: the `^` under a syntax error pointed too far left when double-width characters, like CJK text, came before it on the line.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/bfa1209e35663056248406661f1b90851e5c72fa -->

- Fixed: in JIT-optimized functions, `.sort()` on 16 or fewer integers returned the wrong result with a comparator like `(a, b) => (a + 0.5) - (b + 0.5)`. Regression since v1.4.0.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/d940fbe7b9ca970ab24924387c1a68b41d5c3969 -->

- Fixed: `navigator.hardwareConcurrency`, `os.availableParallelism()` and `process.constrainedMemory()` ignored cgroup v2 limits on Linux hosts that also have a cgroup v1 hierarchy, even just `name=systemd`. Bun's thread counts and GC heap sizing ignored them too.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/b63ebeff30a3533acfa03517a4bc111d48217325 -->

- Fixed: an error thrown right after `let copy = value` at the top of a block could report an earlier statement's line and column, in functions with more than ~110 constants.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/963452075e9d7e2a47a482f297143af5ed4f76c0 -->

- Fixed: `CallSite#getColumnNumber()` counted columns from 0 instead of 1. With `@cspotcode/source-map-support` installed, reading `error.stack` threw "`column` must be greater than or equal to 0" for a frame at column 1.
- Fixed: `error.stack` left out the column of a frame at column 1, printing `file.js:3` instead of `file.js:3:1`.
- Fixed: a stack frame at `const x = require("./x")` pointed at `x` instead of the `require()` call.
- Fixed: an undefined JSX component was reported at its closing tag instead of its opening tag.
- Fixed: the source preview of an uncaught error on the last line of a file with no trailing newline left that line out.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/6f58f6b89446918c534223c3c32df7feec62abea -->

### bun --hot and bun --watch

- Fixed: various stability issues in `bun --hot` and `bun --watch`.

- Fixed: on macOS and Linux, timers under `bun --hot` stopped firing after an uncaught exception, even after you saved a fix. Reloading also resets the exit code to 0.

### bun run

- Fixed: various stability issues in `bun run`, `bunx` and module resolution.

- Fixed: when running as PID 1 in a container, `bun` now exits with 128 + the signal number on Ctrl+C or `docker stop`.

### Transpiler

- Fixed: various stability issues in `Bun.Transpiler` and TypeScript decorators.

- Fixed: `@dec static {}` was accepted. A decorator on a class static block is now a syntax error, like in TypeScript and esbuild.

- Fixed: with standard decorators, when a class decorator returned a new class, the class name inside the class body (decorator arguments, static fields, methods) still referred to the original class.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/5738e23e04cd537ad0076ada37ca530bf8f04a96 -->

- Fixed: hexadecimal, octal and binary number literals above 2^53 could round to the wrong double. For example, `0xb3c8bf81fdf2247` was a different number than in Node.js. `Bun.JSONC.parse()` had the same bug.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/d4be9e3e54e665fd285bd682f5679583f6093bbe -->

- Fixed: `Bun.Transpiler` with `exports.eliminate` left behind imports that only the eliminated exports used. With `trimUnusedImports: false` the imports were kept, and TypeScript output was left with a bare `import "pkg"`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/3469eb3f863daa34bfcac4fb5ebf15705a1cb404 -->

### bun check

- Fixed: a stability issue in `bun check`.

- Fixed: `bun check` reported false TS2456 and TS2502 circularity errors on Slate's `CustomTypes` module augmentation (`Editor: BaseEditor & ReactEditor`). That turned `Editor` into `any` and hid real errors.
- Fixed: some `bun check` errors depended on the number of threads, like a false TS2321 ("Excessive stack depth comparing types") with `@sinclair/typebox` on two or more threads.
- Improved: `bun check` follows TypeScript 7.1 and no longer reports TS2321. After 100 nested comparisons, it assumes the types are related.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/6bb5dc1956505dd1113455f58d4757c924f3ad54 -->

- Fixed: `bun check` reported TS18046 and TS7006 errors that `tsc` doesn't when narrowing the result of `.then()` on a `Promise<T> | PromiseLike<T>` with `"catch" in result`. This affected tRPC.
- Fixed: `bun check` reported a false TS2589 ("excessively deep") on a call that left out an optional parameter whose type is infinitely deep, like TanStack Router's `useLoaderData()` on recursive JSON data.
- Fixed: `bun check` reported a false TS2589 ("excessively deep") when an object built with a spread, inside a class or generic function, went through a chain of generic calls, like in ts-pattern.
- Fixed: `bun check` reported a false TS2615 ("circularly references itself in mapped type") after a type guard narrowed a class whose method takes immer's `Draft<this>`.
- Fixed: `bun check` reported false TS2344, TS2345, TS2339 and TS7031 errors for some generic types that refer to each other in a cycle and use `infer`.
- Fixed: `bun check` reported a false TS2322 when assigning to a union of intersections where one member holds an unresolved conditional type whose constraint is `never`.
- Fixed: `bun check` reported a false TS2322 when a generic function typed through a generic alias (`Id<string>`) is passed to a generic wrapper and the result is assigned to the same alias.
- Fixed: `bun check` reported a false TS2554 when a class method calls an imported function that has the same name as a type parameter and a method of that class.
- Fixed: `bun check` reported an extra TS2322 on the `return` of a function whose return type annotation references itself, on top of TS2577.
- Fixed: `bun check` reported a TS7023 error that `tsc` doesn't for a generator without a return type that yields a variable in a loop and reassigns it from a call to itself.
- Fixed: `bun check` gave a class declared in a loop a wider type than `tsc` when its `extends` expression reads a variable the loop reassigns, which could produce a TS2322 that `tsc` doesn't report.
- Fixed: `bun check` reported TS7022 where `tsc` reports TS2339 for a destructured parameter with contextual type `unknown` whose default reads another binding, like `take({ first, second = first })`.
- Fixed: `bun check` printed `{0}` in place of the file names in TS18000 when `tsconfig.json` files extend each other circularly.
- Fixed: `bun check` missed errors that `tsc` reports while inferring the type of a variable that's reassigned in a loop, like TS2322 on `last = last.next = item`. This also covers TS2367, TS2774, TS2349 and TS2344.
- Fixed: `bun check` missed TS2367 on a comparison like `y === 5` (with `y: string`) in a value assigned to a loop variable that is read earlier in the loop body.
- Fixed: `bun check` missed TS7022 when a loop reassigns its variable from a value that depends on that variable through a class property, or from a `for...of` variable, like `const { children } = current; for (const child of children) current = child`.
- Fixed: `bun check` missed TS2502 for a setter whose parameter annotation reads the property it declares, like `set degrees(value: (Celsius | Kelvin)["degrees"])`.
- Fixed: `bun check` missed TS2589 when a generic function with a self-referential constraint was passed to a generic call, so a `// @ts-expect-error` above it was flagged as unused.
- Fixed: `bun check` missed TS2540 and TS2704 for a `readonly` property when its type is intersected with a mapped type that removes `readonly`, like `Writable<I> & I`.
- Fixed: `bun check` missed TS2445 and TS2341 for a `protected` or `private` property read through an intersection of its class with a mapped type, like `Record<"balance", unknown> & Account`.
- Fixed: `bun check` took quadratic time in the number of keys of any object in `tsconfig.json`, usually `paths`. 40,000 keys took 10.9 s and now take 0.1 s.
- Fixed: `bun check` took quadratic time when thousands of `paths` or `files` entries in `tsconfig.json` each had an error. 4,000 TS5090 errors took 35.5 s and now take 0.04 s.
- Fixed: `bun check` was slower when the project's directory had tens of thousands of sibling files, like in `$TMPDIR` or a large `~/code`.
- Improved: `bun check -b` parses a shared base `tsconfig.json` once for all projects that extend it. 1,000 projects extending 5,000 `paths` went from 71 s and 3.08 GB to 1.6 s and 0.62 GB.
- Improved: `bun check -b` checks small projects in parallel. It runs up to 16 projects at once instead of 4, so a monorepo of large projects uses more memory.
- Improved: `bun check --no-script` runs the type checker even if `package.json` has a `check` script. It accepts the type checker's flags (`bun check --no-script -b`). `bun fmt` also accepts `--no-script`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/b92e2f4704824ad8f28509bda363989add0818c7 -->

### bun install

- Fixed: various stability issues in `bun install`, `bun update`, `bun outdated` and `bun run`.

#### Installing

- Fixed: with the hoisted linker, a dependency removed from `package.json` stayed in `node_modules` after `bun install`, along with packages that only it depended on.
- Fixed: with the isolated linker, a dependency stayed linked in `node_modules` and `.bin` after it was manually deleted from `package.json`, or removed with `bun remove` inside a workspace or while another package still depended on it.
- Fixed: switching between the hoisted and isolated linkers left parts of both layouts in `node_modules`, plus a `.old_modules-*` copy of the old tree.
- Fixed: an install that was killed partway could leave a half-written package in `node_modules` that later installs treated as installed.
- Fixed: with the hoisted linker, a `file:` folder outside the project (`file:../plugin`) couldn't load its own dependencies, and on Windows the install failed with `EPERM`.
- Fixed: `file:` folders and local tarballs were reinstalled on every `bun install` with the hoisted linker.
- Fixed: without a lockfile, `bun install --production` failed when a `workspace:`, `link:` or `file:` devDependency pointed to a missing folder, like when a Docker image only contains one package from a monorepo.
- Fixed: `bun install` failed with `Failed to link <pkg>: EEXIST` on an up-to-date `node_modules` that's mounted read-only.
- Fixed: `bun install --dry-run` ran the project's lifecycle scripts, and `dryRun = true` in `bunfig.toml` was ignored.
- Fixed: `bun install --dry-run` printed one line per dependency edge, skipped peers and ignored the platform. It now lists each package the install would add to `node_modules` once.
- Fixed: `bun install --analyze` and `bun add --analyze` skipped packages that are only imported by subpath, like `lodash/debounce`.
- Fixed: with the isolated linker, an optional dependency whose tarball couldn't be downloaded failed the install. It's now skipped.
- Fixed: `bun install <pkg>`, `bun link` and `bun update -i` exited with code 0 after printing `Failed to install N packages`.
- Fixed: a relative `--cwd` was applied twice by `bun update`, `bun link`, `bun unlink` and `bun why`, so they failed with `ENOENT`.
- Fixed: `bun install` left extraction directories in `$TMPDIR` when two installs shared a cache or a tarball failed to extract, which filled the disk on long-lived CI machines.
- Fixed: two installs sharing a cache on NFS could delete each other's entries and fail with `ENOENT`.
- Fixed: with `NODE_ENV=development` or `test`, `bun install` read `.env.production` instead of the `.env` files that `bun run` reads.
- Fixed: `bun --bun run` only worked for the first user on a shared machine.
- Fixed: on Alpine Linux (musl), `Bun.which()` returned a file that isn't executable.

#### Resolving versions

- Fixed: `1.0.0 || ^2.0.0` resolved to `1.0.0`. A range that starts with an exact version was parsed as only that version.
- Fixed: `bun add`, `bun install` and `bun update --latest` failed for a package whose `latest` dist-tag is missing or points to an unpublished version. They now fall back to the highest release.
- Fixed: dist-tags that start with a digit, such as `pkg@1beta`, were parsed as version ranges.
- Fixed: an auto-installed peer dependency got the newest version that one dependent allows. It now gets the newest version that all of them accept.
- Fixed: a peer dependency on `bun` downloaded the `bun` npm package, which is 80 to 170 MB.
- Fixed: a version published after Bun cached the package's metadata couldn't be installed for up to 5 minutes.
- Fixed: in a monorepo with a lockfile, adding a dependency whose name another workspace uses for an `npm:` alias requested a garbled name, such as `GET /1.0.0no-deps - 404`.
- Fixed: editing a workspace's `package.json` re-downloaded its GitHub and tarball dependencies and re-fetched its git dependencies, even though `bun.lock` had already resolved them.
- Fixed: `file:`, tarball and git packages with no `name` in their `package.json` got broken `bun.lock` entries. They're now named after their source.
- Fixed: an `overrides` key with a prerelease range, such as `pkg@>=5.0.0-alpha.0 <8`, also replaced dependencies on `^4`.
- Fixed: `bun add foo` and `bun update --latest` installed a version that a version-scoped override like `"foo@>=2.0.0": "1.2.0"` forbids.
- Fixed: `Bun.semver.satisfies()` returned `true` for versions that aren't valid semver, such as `""`, `"1.2.3.4"` and `"1.2.3 junk"`, and `false` for `1.0.0+build-1` against `^1.0.0`.
- Fixed: `Bun.semver.satisfies()` and `bun install` parsed build metadata after a bare major (`^2+x`) as a second range, which allowed a different major version.
- Fixed: `Bun.semver.order("2+1", "2.0.0")` threw.
- Fixed: `>=0.5 0` was parsed as two alternatives instead of an intersection, and `<x` and `>x` matched every version.

#### Hoisted and isolated linkers

- Fixed: the hoisted linker could place a package next to a version of its peer dependency that's outside the peer's range.
- Fixed: with the hoisted linker, `--filter`, `--production`, `--omit`, `--os` and `--cpu` changed where packages were placed. Switching flags could leave a workspace loading the wrong version. Placement now only depends on `bun.lock`.
- Fixed: with the hoisted linker, a dependency nested under a package with `bundledDependencies` could load the bundled copy instead of the version it asked for.
- Fixed: with the hoisted linker, `bun prune` deleted a package's bundled dependencies when `bun.lock` didn't mark them as bundled, which affected `aws-cdk-lib`.
- Fixed: `bun add -g` didn't link the package's binaries into the global bin folder when `linker = "isolated"` was set in `~/.bunfig.toml`.
- Fixed: with the isolated linker, packages that are peer dependencies of each other were installed twice when different workspaces or dependencies pulled them in.
- Fixed: with the isolated linker and an `npm:` alias that installs a second copy of a package, `node_modules/.bun/node_modules/<name>` could point at a different version after each install.
- Fixed: the isolated linker replaced a symlinked `node_modules` with a real folder. Both linkers now install through the symlink, and cleanup doesn't delete anything behind it.
- Fixed: with the isolated linker on macOS and Linux, a workspace whose folder or parent folder is a symlink ended up with dangling dependency symlinks.
- Fixed: the isolated linker silently dropped symlinks inside a `file:` folder dependency. Both linkers now keep symlinks that point inside the folder, copy symlinks to other project files as regular files, and skip the rest with a warning.
- Fixed: with `globalStore = true`, TypeScript couldn't find the project's `@types/*` from inside a shared package.
- Fixed: `BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_STORE=false` (also `no`, `off` and an empty value) enabled the global store.
- Fixed: symlinks to a renamed or removed workspace were left in `node_modules`.
- Fixed: with the hoisted linker, `bun install` didn't link a newly added workspace when the registry package of the same name and version was already in `node_modules`.
- Fixed: on Alpine Linux, a package that ships native binaries for both libcs, such as `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`, could have its command linked to the glibc binary.
- Fixed: none of a package's binaries were linked if one value in its `bin` object wasn't a string.
- Fixed: when several packages declare the same binary, which one ended up in `.bin` was arbitrary. Direct dependencies now take priority.
- Fixed: a binary that's generated by the package's own install script, like a workspace CLI built in `prepare`, wasn't linked into `.bin` until the next `bun install`.
- Fixed: `bun install` failed on file systems that don't support symlinks. It now warns once and skips the `.bin` links.

#### Lockfile and `--frozen-lockfile`

- Fixed: a fresh `bun install` could write a different `bun.lock` depending on which registry response arrived first. Dependencies are now resolved in a deterministic order.
- Fixed: `bun ci` failed in an unchanged monorepo when a workspace had a lifecycle script and a dependency on `latest`, as soon as a newer version of that dependency was published.
- Fixed: `bun ci` applied `minimumReleaseAge` to a version already pinned in `bun.lock` and failed when `package.json` expressed the same version differently, such as with `catalog:`.
- Fixed: a direct dependency locked at a version outside its `package.json` range, which can happen after a bad merge, was installed anyway and passed `--frozen-lockfile`.
- Fixed: `bun install` kept a locked version that an `overrides` rule forbids, which can also happen after a bad merge. It now re-resolves that entry, and `--frozen-lockfile` fails with an explanation.
- Fixed: `bun install` could write a `bun.lock` it couldn't read back (`Failed to resolve prod dependency`) when a package bundles a package that another package lists as an optional peer.
- Fixed: `bun <file>.lockb` printed the lockfile from the file's directory instead of the file itself. That broke using it as a git `textconv`, where git passes a temporary copy.
- Fixed: `bun pm migrate` left `trustedDependencies` out of the `bun.lock` it wrote, so `bun pm untrusted` listed trusted packages as blocked.
- Fixed: a `yarn.lock` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` that pins a GitHub dependency failed on the first `bun install` and lost the pin on the second. The pinned commit is now installed, including for pnpm's `type: git` resolutions.
- Fixed: migrating a Yarn v1 lockfile failed with "failed to resolve" on `link:` and bare path (`./dir`) entries, and in a monorepo where a registry package depends on a workspace.
- Fixed: migrating a Yarn v1 lockfile merged a tarball or hosted-git entry with the registry package of the same name and version, so a fork was replaced by the published package.
- Fixed: a lockfile that Bun can't migrate, like npm 6's `package-lock.json`, prevented Bun from migrating a `yarn.lock` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` next to it. Bun now warns and tries the next one.
- Fixed: a single `package-lock.json` entry from another host without an `integrity` made Bun ignore the whole lockfile. The entry now keeps its version and gets its integrity from the configured registry, with a warning.

#### Workspaces and catalogs

- Fixed: a workspace whose `package.json` has no `name` failed the whole install. It's now skipped.
- Fixed: depending on `latest` of a sibling workspace that isn't published failed with a 404. It now links the workspace.
- Fixed: a workspace was left out of the install when the root `package.json` depends on a registry package with the same name. It now keeps its `bun.lock` entry and its dependencies are installed.
- Fixed: `bun add <name>` inside a workspace installed the package from the registry when `<name>` is also a sibling workspace. It now links the workspace and writes `workspace:*`.
- Fixed: `bun add alias@npm:<workspace>` wrote `"alias": "workspace:*"`, which every later install rejected.
- Fixed: `bun link <package>` inside a workspace that has `workspace:` or `catalog:` dependencies failed with `Workspace dependency "bar" not found` or `is not in the catalog`.
- Fixed: negated `workspaces` entries written as `!./pkg` or `!pkg/` were ignored, and `bun run --filter` and `--workspaces` didn't apply negated entries.
- Fixed: workspace globs skipped symlinked directories.
- Fixed: `bun update <name>` rewrote non-registry entries in `package.json`, for example `workspace:^` to `workspace:*`.
- Fixed: `bun run --filter <pkg> deploy` still ran `deploy` and `postdeploy` after `predeploy` failed. It now skips them, like `bun run` without `--filter`.

#### Registries, `.npmrc` and `bunfig.toml`

- Fixed: a registry URL with a path and no trailing slash, such as `https://host/npm/repo`, lost its last path segment, so every request got a 404.
- Fixed: `.npmrc` credentials are now matched the same way npm matches them. A `//host/` entry applies to every path under it, including a registry set by `--registry` or an environment variable.
- Fixed: `~` in `cache.dir`, `globalDir`, `globalBinDir` and `cafile` created a directory literally named `~`.
- Fixed: a relative `cafile`, `cache`, `globalDir` or `globalBinDir` in `bunfig.toml` or `.npmrc` is now resolved relative to that file. A relative `cafile` used to only work from the project root.
- Fixed: a relative `--config`, `--cache-dir` or `--cafile` is now resolved relative to the current working directory instead of the project root.
- Fixed: `-g` commands ignored `globalDir` from `--config` and `~/.bunfig.toml`.
- Fixed: `bun publish` and `bun pm whoami` ignored `http_proxy`. Those two and `bun audit` also ignored `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0`.
- Fixed: a redirected registry request ignored `NO_PROXY` for the new URL. Each redirect now picks its proxy based on its own URL, like `fetch()`.
- Fixed: credentials embedded in a registry URL were sent percent-encoded, so `p%40ss` wasn't sent as `p@ss`.
- Fixed: `BUN_CONFIG_MAX_HTTP_REQUESTS` was ignored.

#### Tarballs and the cache

- Fixed: `--force` and re-adding the same path or URL kept the old contents of a tarball dependency, and `bun update` left its old hash in `bun.lock`.
- Fixed: `file:` and URL tarballs were cached by path or URL, so two projects or branches with different files at the same path got each other's package.
- Fixed: two registries on the same host that differ only in port, path or protocol shared cache entries.
- Fixed: uncompressed `.tar` packages of 2 MB or more, and `.tgz` files of that size served with `Content-Encoding: gzip`, failed to install.
- Fixed: `Bun.Archive`'s `extract(dir, { glob })` and `files()` resolved with the entries read so far on a truncated or corrupted archive. They now reject, like `extract(dir)`.

#### Git dependencies

- Improved: git dependencies now require Git 2.24 or newer.
- Fixed: a cached git dependency never picked up tags and branches pushed after it was cached. Bumping to a new tag failed with `no commit matching`, and `bun update` stayed on the old commit.
- Fixed: `git+ssh://git@host:2222/...` lost its port when Bun fell back to ssh.
- Fixed: a git dependency with an ssh URL never fell back to ssh when the https attempt returned "not found".
- Fixed: `bun add name@git+ssh://host/repo.git` failed with `unrecognised dependency format` for hosts other than GitHub.
- Fixed: `deploy@host:org/repo.git` was cloned as `git@deploy@host`.
- Fixed: `gitlab:`, `bitbucket:`, `gist:` and `sourcehut:` dependencies failed to install from `bun.lock` on a clean machine. They're now written as `git+ssh://git@gitlab.com/user/repo#<sha>`, and existing entries still install.
- Fixed: an optional git dependency that can't be cloned failed the install. It's now skipped with a warning.
- Fixed: `bun install` and `bun create` run from a git hook operated on the hook's repository, because `GIT_DIR` and similar variables were passed on to git.
- Fixed: `bun install` overrode your `core.sshCommand` or `core.askPass` for git dependencies when it's set outside `~/.gitconfig`, like in `~/.config/git/config` or an included file.
- Fixed: `submodule.recurse = true` in your git config broke a git dependency that has a submodule.
- Fixed: a cached clone that git can't use, because of a stale lock file or a damaged ref store, failed every install. It's now re-cloned.

#### Lifecycle scripts and trust

- Fixed: with the isolated linker, a package added to `trustedDependencies` after it was installed never ran its scripts.
- Fixed: a package installed through an `npm:` alias couldn't be trusted consistently. It's now trusted by its real name in `package.json`, `--trust`, `bun pm trust` and `bun.lock`.
- Fixed: `--concurrent-scripts` and `concurrentScripts` had no effect with the isolated linker, and the `bunfig.toml` value took precedence over the flag.
- Fixed: `bun pm untrusted`, `bun pm trust` and `bun pm ls --trusted` used a stale lockfile instead of `package.json`.
- Fixed: `bun pm pack`, `bun publish` and `bun pm version` ran lifecycle scripts without `node_modules/.bin` in `PATH`, so `"prepack": "tsc"` failed with `command not found`.
- Fixed: a regression in Bun v1.4.0 where a failed lifecycle script's non-UTF-8 output, such as Latin-1 or Shift-JIS compiler errors, was printed with every invalid byte replaced by U+FFFD.

#### `bun add`, `bun remove`, `bun update` and `bun outdated`

- Fixed: removing the last package in a dependency group with `bun remove` reordered the other keys in `package.json`.
- Fixed: `bun add ../path` run from a subdirectory of the project, and `bun install -g .`, resolved the path from the wrong directory.
- Fixed: `bun add` with a folder, tarball or git URL wrote the package into `bun.lock` twice when `package.json` already listed it from another source.
- Fixed: the first `bun add -g` on a machine edited a `package.json` above the global directory, such as `~/package.json`.
- Fixed: `bun add --dry-run` in an empty directory created a `package.json`.
- Fixed: `bun add -E react@18` wrote `18`. `--exact` now pins the range you typed to the installed version, like npm.
- Fixed: `bun add`, `bun remove`, `bun update` and `bun patch` rewrote `package.json` even when nothing changed.
- Fixed: commands that rewrite `package.json` turned control characters in strings into `\x1B` or `\v`, which isn't valid JSON.
- Fixed: `bun update` printed `(no changes)` when it had rewritten `package.json`.
- Fixed: `bun update --latest` downgraded a dependency written as a dist-tag like `"canary"` when that tag is ahead of `latest`. `bun update -i` no longer offers an older `latest` either.
- Fixed: `bun update --latest` downgraded a `catalog` entry that was ahead of the `latest` tag. This affected pinned versions, ranges and dist-tags like `canary`.
- Fixed: `bun update --interactive` rewrote ranges like `>=1.0.0 <2`, `1.x` and `^1 || ^2` as their first character plus the chosen version. They're now left unchanged if they already allow the chosen version.
- Fixed: `bun update --exact` pinned `peerDependencies` ranges, and `bun update --latest` narrowed a peer range that already allows the latest version.
- Fixed: `bun outdated a b` only listed packages matching both patterns. It now lists packages matching either one, and `!pattern` excludes.
- Fixed: `bun outdated` hid dependencies that are ahead of the `latest` tag. It now lists them if `bun update` would change them.

#### `bun pm` and `bun why`

- Fixed: `bun pm bin -g` and `bun pm ls -g` failed with `No package.json was found` before the first global install.
- Fixed: `bun pm ls` listed the lockfile's packages under a `node_modules` label. When `node_modules` exists, it now lists what's actually installed.
- Fixed: `bun why name@version` found nothing for exact versions, scoped names and workspaces.
- Fixed: `bun why` printed a package's dependents again at every occurrence, which grew exponentially in large trees. Repeats are now marked `*deduped`.
- Fixed: `bun pm version` didn't create a commit or tag in a git worktree or submodule, where `.git` is a file.
- Fixed: `bun pm version <increment>` now computes the same version as `npm version`. `1.0.0-rc.1` plus `major` is `1.0.0`, not `2.0.0`, and `v2.0.0` is written as `2.0.0`.
- Fixed: `bun pm view pkg@tag` silently used `latest` for a dist-tag that doesn't exist. It's now an error that lists the available tags.
- Fixed: `bun pm cache rm` deleted the cache directory itself, which left a dangling link when it's a symlink and failed with `EACCES` in a read-only parent.
- Fixed: `bun pm cache rm` printed `Cleared 'bun install' cache` without deleting anything when `~/.bunfig.toml` set the cache directory.

#### `bun pm pack` and `bun publish`

- Fixed: `workspace:` and `catalog:` versions came from `bun.lock`, so they could be stale, and packing failed without a lockfile. They now come from the `package.json` files.
- Fixed: a `catalog:` dependency whose catalog entry is `workspace:^` or another `workspace:` form was published as-is. It's now replaced with the workspace's version.
- Fixed: `bun pm pack` and `bun publish` omitted `bundledDependencies` with the isolated linker and in workspaces.
- Fixed: `!pattern` in `.npmignore` couldn't re-include files below an excluded directory.
- Fixed: relative `--destination` and `--filename` paths, and `bun publish ./x.tgz`, were resolved from the package root instead of the current directory.
- Fixed: `bun publish --provenance`, `publishConfig.provenance` and `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` were ignored, so the package was published without provenance. They're now errors until Bun supports generating it.
- Fixed: a file listed under several `bin` names was packed several times.

#### `bun patch`

- Fixed: a patch that adds a file in a new directory failed with `EACCES` for non-root users.
- Fixed: hunks were applied by line number alone, so a patch could land in the wrong place after the file changed. They're now matched by context, like `git apply`.
- Fixed: a patch that appends lines to a file lost the last line when the file has no trailing newline before or after the change.
- Fixed: `bun patch --commit` on an already patched package wrote `.bun-tag` files and cache paths into the patch.
- Fixed: `bun patch` dropped the package's bundled and nested dependencies, and `--commit` recorded them as deleted.
- Fixed: a `bun patch` that failed partway left a partial package, or none, in `node_modules`.
- Fixed: a `bun patch --commit` whose patch doesn't apply, or whose install is refused, could leave the package folder, `package.json` or `bun.lock` changed. Now nothing is modified until every check has passed.
- Fixed: with the isolated linker, `bun patch` replaced `node_modules/<pkg>` with a directory that couldn't load its dependencies.
- Fixed: `bun patch` and `bun patch --commit` failed with `ENOENT` when the package is installed but no longer in the cache, for example after `bun pm cache rm`.
- Fixed: `bun patch --commit` failed when a patched file or the cache folder has a non-ASCII name.
- Fixed: `bun install` silently skipped the parts of a patch it can't apply, like a `Binary files ... differ` section, and a `patchedDependencies` key without a version. Each one now prints a warning.

#### `bunx`

- Fixed: `bunx pkg@latest` relinked everything on every run, and a copy more than a day old was refreshed on every run.
- Fixed: several `bunx <pkg>` processes started at the same time corrupted their shared install.
- Fixed: `bunx <tool>` with a cached copy older than a day failed when the registry returned 5xx, 429 or 408, or when a newer version's tarball couldn't be fetched.
- Fixed: `bunx pkg@3` failed with `could not determine executable to run` in a project where another version of `pkg` is installed and has no such command.
- Fixed: `bunx @scope/pkg` could run another package's `.bin` entry of the same name instead of that package's own command.

#### `bun create`

- Fixed: `bun create <local template> <dir>` deleted an existing directory. It now merges, lists conflicts and only overwrites with `--force`.
- Fixed: `git init` and the first commit raced the template's tasks and `bun install`. The first commit now contains exactly the template.
- Fixed: `bun-create` tasks ran without a shell, didn't run at all in a template without dependencies, and their failures were ignored.
- Fixed: the indentation of the template's `package.json` was lost.

#### Auto-install

- Fixed: timers and I/O callbacks could run inside `require()`, `import()` and `Bun.resolveSync()` while auto-install fetched a package.
- Fixed: importing a second version (`pkg@2` after `pkg@1`) failed with `Unexpected` when the package's metadata was in the disk cache.
- Fixed: one failed auto-install download limited `fetch()` to 4 concurrent requests for the rest of the process.
- Fixed: peer dependencies of auto-installed packages failed with "Cannot find module".
- Fixed: with auto-install, an import throws "Cannot find package" when the cache or temp directory can't be written, like in a read-only container.

#### Windows

- Fixed: commands whose shebang uses `env -S` didn't run.
- Fixed: `.bunx` shims broke when the package is on another drive.
- Fixed: `bun remove` left `.bunx` and `.exe` shims behind.
- Fixed: `bun install` failed in the root of a drive.
- Fixed: `EINVAL: Failed to replace old lockfile` on exFAT and FAT32 drives.
- Fixed: renames failed while a virus scanner held a new file open. They're now retried for up to 5 seconds.
- Fixed: `bun create <local template>` failed with "ENOENT: failed to copy file" when the working directory, the template or the destination has a non-ASCII character.
- Fixed: the `preversion`, `version` and `postversion` scripts of `bun pm version` ran with an empty environment in a git repository.

### JavaScript bundler

- Fixed: various stability issues in `bun build`, `Bun.build` plugins and macros.

- Fixed: `bun build --minify` gave two default exports the same name when each was a parenthesized named function or class expression, like `export default (function inc() {})`.
- Fixed: `bun build` left an HTML `<img src>` pointing to the source path without writing the file when a stylesheet inlined the same image through `url()`.

- Fixed: in source maps from `bun build --react-compiler`, `catch` and the `{` after it mapped to the position of `try`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/491aaad15f493db96ad83da99592e45815bf75be -->

- Fixed: `bun build` source maps mapped `export default function`, `export default class`, `export async function`, `abstract class`, `import()`, `require()` and `require.resolve()` to the wrong column.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/6f58f6b89446918c534223c3c32df7feec62abea -->

### bun build --compile

- Fixed: various stability issues in `bun build --compile` and compiled executables.

### CSS Parser

- Fixed: a stability issue in the CSS parser.

- Fixed: `bun build` dropped `translate`, `rotate` or `scale` declared before `transform` in the same CSS rule, and merged the ones declared after it into `transform`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/3da4e2541270d5a859fc1630ec58042f369f525e -->

### Dev server

- Fixed: a stability issue in the dev server.

- Fixed: `bun ./index.html` ignored `--port 3000` and `--host 0.0.0.0` when written with a space instead of `=`.
- Fixed: `bun ./index.html --host=::1` threw a `RangeError`.
- Fixed: `bun ./index.html` printed a startup error twice, such as the one for an invalid `--port`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/ed680823cb629699012188c9eb38907df7876e52 -->

- Fixed: the underline under a CSS resolve error for `url('/fonts/a.woff2')` ended 5 characters early. It now covers the whole `url(...)`, and only the path in `composes: x from "./a.css"`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/91e7e3b140eaef348b7bc33d564dcb67b7de4ddd -->

### bun test

- Fixed: various stability issues in `bun test` and `bun test --changed`.

- Fixed: `bun test --update-snapshots` emptied a snapshot file when the run ended early, like with `--bail`. The old contents are now kept until the new ones are written.

- Fixed: `bun test --coverage` counted skipped code as covered: the right side of `||`, `&&`, `??` or `?:` on its own line, code skipped by `?.`, `||=`, `&&=`, `??=` or an unused default value, and an untaken `break`.
- Fixed: `bun test --coverage` counted the lines after an `await` or `yield` as covered when the function never resumed past it. `% Lines` can drop after upgrading, so check your `coverageThreshold`.
- Fixed: `bun test --coverage` listed the wrong `Uncovered Line #s` for a function that never ran. The range could start two lines early and miss the last line.
- Fixed: `bun test --coverage` reported lines that ran as uncovered, such as a `break` in a block inside `while (true)`, or the `import` above `class Derived extends Base() {}`.
- Fixed: `bun test --coverage` ignored a line with only `default:`, or `case` with its value on the next line, in functions that ran.
- Fixed: `bun test --coverage` listed the `{` line instead of the `else` line when `else` and `{` were on separate lines. Source maps gave `else` the position of the statement after it.
- Fixed: `bun test --coverage` listed lines at the top of a file as code, comments included, when the file used a `--define` name whose value is a non-empty object or array.
- Fixed: `% Funcs` in `bun test --coverage` counted implicit constructors, class field initializers, `static` blocks, and generator and async function bodies as functions. A fully tested class could show 50%.
- Fixed: the `DA:` hit counts in `lcov.info` weren't the number of times a line ran. A line that ran once could show 14.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/6f58f6b89446918c534223c3c32df7feec62abea -->

### Bun Shell

- Fixed: a stability issue in Bun Shell.

- Fixed: `` $`cmd` `` truncated an environment variable's value at a NUL byte. `.env()` and `.cwd()` now throw `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` for strings containing a NUL byte.
- Fixed: in Bun Shell, `mv -n` overwrote an existing destination.
- Fixed: in Bun Shell, `cp -n` exited with code 1 when the destination existed.

### SQL

- Fixed: various stability issues in `Bun.SQL`, `bun:sqlite` and `node:sqlite`.

#### `Bun.SQL` connection pool

- Fixed: `idleTimeout` and `maxLifetime` closed a connection that was running a query, was reserved, or had an open `sql.begin()` transaction. Now the connection finishes its work first.
- Fixed: a pool that lost some of its connections didn't open new ones as long as one was still usable, so it never grew back to `max`.
- Fixed: a connection released to the pool inside an open transaction, such as a reservation after a manual `BEGIN`, was handed to the next caller. The pool now closes it.
- Fixed: `sql.close({ timeout: 0 })` waited for running queries instead of closing immediately.
- Fixed: `sql.close({ timeout: 2 ** 31 })` overflowed the timer and killed the running queries after 1 ms.
- Fixed: `sql.begin()` and `sql.reserve()` jumped ahead of older queries that were waiting for a connection. Callers are now served in FIFO order.
- Fixed: `onconnect` and `onclose` never fired for the `sql.listen()` connection.
- Improved: PostgreSQL and MySQL sockets now use TCP keepalive (60 seconds), so a query fails instead of waiting forever when the server disappears.

#### `Bun.SQL` transactions

- Fixed: in `sql.begin(tx => Promise.all(tasks))`, after one task failed, statements that the other tasks sent after the `ROLLBACK` ran in autocommit mode, so their rows were kept. They now reject.
- Fixed: a query created on a `reserved` or `tx` handle but first awaited after `release()`, `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` ran on a connection that could belong to another caller. It now rejects.
- Fixed: `reserved.release()` during a running `reserved.begin()` returned the connection early, so that transaction's `COMMIT` could commit the next caller's work.
- Fixed: `tx.close({ timeout })` committed the transaction when its queries finished in time. It now rolls back.
- Fixed: the `sql.begin()` callback saw no `AsyncLocalStorage` store on a cold pool, and another request's store on a busy one. It now sees its caller's.
- Fixed: a result returned from a `sql.begin()` or `tx.savepoint()` callback was returned as a plain array without `count` and `command`.
- Fixed: `sql.begin()` and `sql.beginDistributed()` (PostgreSQL, MySQL) rejected a transaction the server had committed or prepared when the server's response and its shutdown error arrived in the same read.

#### `Bun.SQL` queries and results

- Improved: a `` sql`...` `` call compiled by Babel's or swc's loose mode for template literals now throws a `TypeError`. Disable loose mode for template literals.
- Fixed: `affectedRows` was always `null` on PostgreSQL and SQLite. It's now the number of rows written, and `0` for a `SELECT`. On MySQL, `count` was `0` after a write.
- Fixed: `WHERE id IN ${sql([])}` was a syntax error on PostgreSQL and MySQL. It now matches no rows.
- Fixed: on MySQL and MariaDB, `sql("db.table")` quoted the whole string as a single identifier. It's now `` `db`.`table` ``, as documented.
- Fixed: on MySQL, `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE ${sql({ age: 31 })}` was a syntax error when the clause was lowercase or split across lines.
- Fixed: `sql instanceof Bun.SQL` threw a `TypeError`.
- Improved: in TypeScript, the awaited result of a query has `count`, `command`, `affectedRows`, `columns` and the other result properties.

#### `Bun.SQL` connection options

- Improved: `Bun.SQL` no longer reads the `PASSWORD` environment variable. Use `PGPASSWORD`, `MYSQL_PASSWORD`, the URL or the `password` option.
- Fixed: `new SQL({ filename: "./dev.db" })` without `adapter` tried to connect to PostgreSQL, and `SQLITE_URL=x.db` tried to open a file named `postgres://x.db`.
- Fixed: the documented `socket` option and `?socket=` had no effect, and `mysql://user:pass@/db?socket=/path` threw `Invalid URL`.
- Fixed: a `path` that doesn't exist was ignored, and Bun connected over TCP. The connection now fails with `ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_REFUSED` or `ERR_MYSQL_CONNECTION_REFUSED`.
- Fixed: `PGUSERNAME` and `USERNAME` were documented as the PostgreSQL user but ignored.
- Fixed: a `mariadb://` URL without a database tried to select a database named `mariadb` and failed with errno 1049. It no longer selects one.
- Fixed: with the SQLite adapter, `?mode=rw` created the file, and `?mode=RO` or `{ readwrite: false }` opened it read-write.

#### `Bun.SQL` with PostgreSQL

- Fixed: each distinct combination of `NULL` parameters prepared another server-side statement, and none of them were ever closed, so backends grew to several GB. Each connection now keeps its 1,024 most recent statements.
- Fixed: after `ALTER TABLE`, `DEALLOCATE ALL` or `DISCARD ALL`, a cached statement kept failing, for example with `cached plan must not change result type`. Bun now re-prepares it.
- Fixed: `sql.array(["a", "b"])` without a type was cast to `JSON[]`, so a `text[]` column stored JSON-quoted elements. Bun no longer adds a cast.
- Fixed: `null` in `sql.array(values, "TEXT")` or `"INT"` became the string `"null"` or an error. It's now SQL `NULL`.
- Fixed: a prepared query that returned an `int4[]` or `float4[]` with a `NULL` or more than one dimension rejected with `ERR_POSTGRES_NULLS_IN_ARRAY_NOT_SUPPORTED_YET` or `ERR_POSTGRES_MULTIDIMENSIONAL_ARRAY_NOT_SUPPORTED_YET`.
- Fixed: a `Date` bound to `text` was stored as its `toString()`, and a plain object as `[object Object]`. They're now stored as ISO 8601 and JSON.
- Fixed: a `Date` bound to `date` or `time` failed.
- Fixed: with `prepare: false`, a `Date` was sent as its `toString()`, and an object bound to `jsonb` as `[object Object]`.
- Fixed: an array or object bound to a `bool`, `int4`, `float8` or `timestamp` parameter was coerced on the client, so `[]` became `true`. It's now sent as text and validated by the server.
- Fixed: an Invalid Date was stored as 1970-01-01 on PostgreSQL and MySQL. The query now rejects.
- Fixed: whole numbers from 2^51 to 2^53 - 1 were sent as `float8`, so `numeric` stored 2^52 + 1 as `4503599627370500`. They're now sent as `int8`, which Bun returns as a string.
- Fixed: `COPY ... FROM STDIN` and `COPY ... TO STDOUT` as plain queries, without a stream, now reject with `ERR_POSTGRES_COPY_NOT_SUPPORTED`.
- Fixed: `PostgresError.column` and `.line` pointed to a position in Bun's own source code when the server didn't send one.

#### `Bun.SQL` with MySQL and MariaDB

- Fixed: queries on the same connection were sent one at a time instead of pipelined, a regression since v1.2.22. With 30 ms of latency, four prepared queries now take 31 ms, down from 124 ms.
- Fixed: without TLS, `caching_sha2_password` logins failed with errno 1045 for passwords of 20 bytes or more. Fast authentication also never succeeded, so plain TCP needed `allowPublicKeyRetrieval: true` on every login.
- Fixed: `sha256_password` was documented, but every login failed with errno 1045.
- Fixed: a single `INSERT` with K nullable columns could prepare up to 2^K statements on the server, which were never closed. Each connection now keeps its 256 most recent statements.
- Fixed: a failed prepare was cached, so the query kept failing after a `CREATE TABLE` had made it valid.
- Fixed: a query on a connection that had been idle didn't keep the process alive, so the process could exit with code 0 while the query was in flight.
- Fixed: two queries on one connection could resolve with each other's rows when a parameter's `toJSON()` started a query.
- Fixed: MariaDB rejected every object or array parameter with errno 1210.
- Fixed: a `Date` before 1970 was rejected, and a prepared query lost the fractional seconds of `TIME(n)` columns.
- Fixed: `lastInsertRowid` above 2^53 - 1 was rounded. It's now returned as a string, or a `BigInt` with `bigint: true`.
- Fixed: `Bun.SQL` threw `ERR_MYSQL_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION` when a MySQL or MariaDB server rejected a new connection, such as when it hit `max_connections`. It now throws the server's error (`errno` 1040, "Too many connections").

#### `Bun.SQL` with SQLite

- Fixed: a valid query resolved to `[]` when its text was written like `select*from t` or `/*c*/select`, or was `values (...)`.
- Fixed: `INSERT ... SELECT` and `WITH ... INSERT` reported a `count` of 0.
- Fixed: a string of several statements whose first statement returns rows, such as a migration file that starts with a `PRAGMA`, only ran that statement.
- Fixed: a second `sql.begin()` while another one was running failed with `cannot start a transaction within a transaction`. It now waits.
- Fixed: a failed `COMMIT` left the transaction open, so every later `sql.begin()` failed.

#### `bun:sqlite`

- Fixed: `bun:sqlite` lost writes at process exit when `iterate()` on a statement that writes, like `INSERT ... RETURNING`, wasn't read to the end. They're now committed. An explicit `BEGIN` is still rolled back.
- Fixed: `new Database(path, { create: false })` failed with `SQLITE_MISUSE` on an existing file, and so did `{}`, `{ readonly: false }` and `{ readwrite: false }`.
- Fixed: `{ readonly: true, create: true }` opened the database read-write. It now throws a `TypeError`.
- Fixed: `db.run("a; b; c")` and `db.exec()` swallowed runtime errors in every statement except the last. They now throw at the failing statement and skip the rest.
- Fixed: after `ALTER TABLE`, an existing `Statement` returned rows with the old column names, or values under the wrong keys.
- Fixed: `{ name: 1 }` bound `NULL` to `$name` by default, and `{ $name: 1 }` threw with `strict: true`. Both forms now work in both modes.
- Fixed: `db.prepare(sql, "x")` ignored a binding that wasn't an array.
- Fixed: `row["1"]` was `undefined` for `SELECT 1`.
- Fixed: `changes` also counted rows written by triggers, foreign key cascades and FTS5 shadow tables. It now counts the statement's own rows, like `node:sqlite`.
- Fixed: `break` out of a `stmt.iterate()` loop left the cursor open, so a later `DROP TABLE` failed with `database table is locked`.
- Fixed: `db.transaction(fn)` committed when `fn` returned a promise that was already rejected, which is what an `async` function does when it throws before its first `await`. It now rolls back.
- Fixed: `stmt.run(new Date())`, or a `Map` or a `Promise` as the only argument, bound `NULL`. It now throws a `TypeError`.
- Fixed: terminating a Worker during a write with `RETURNING` outside a transaction could commit rows without their full-text (FTS) index entries. `MATCH` then missed those rows. `INSERT INTO ft(ft) VALUES('rebuild')` repairs the index.
- Fixed: `db.query()` cached SQL text of any size, so a loop over multi-megabyte queries with changing text grew to 953 MB. It now peaks at 92 MB.
- Improved: statements now report their native memory to the garbage collector. 20,000 dropped 200-parameter statements hold 27 MB instead of 465 MB.
- Improved: `stmt.get()` stops after the first row instead of reading the whole result. Statements that write (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE … RETURNING`) still apply and commit all their changes.
- Improved: rows with 63 or more columns take 310 instructions per cell, down from 1,665.
- Improved: `db.run()` with a string of 80,000 statements takes 0.11 s of CPU time, down from 5.34 s.
- Improved: Workers no longer share one SQLite malloc mutex. As a result, `PRAGMA hard_heap_limit` and `soft_heap_limit` are accepted but no longer enforced, like in `node:sqlite`.

#### `node:sqlite`

- Fixed: `db.close()` kept the file and its `-wal` and `-shm` files open until every `StatementSync` was garbage collected, which caused `EBUSY` on Windows.
- Fixed: a `Proxy` (Vue `reactive()`, MobX) or a module namespace as named parameters bound `NULL` to every parameter.
- Fixed: `stmt.get()` on `INSERT ... RETURNING` returned a row even though the commit failed on a deferred foreign key. It now throws.
- Improved: `stmt.get()` on a 5-column row takes 4,077 instructions, down from 13,458.

### TypeScript types

- Fixed: `toHaveBeenCalledOnce()` was missing from `bun-types`. The matcher already worked in `bun test`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/bfa1209e35663056248406661f1b90851e5c72fa -->

- Fixed: `@types/bun` typed `Bun.hash()` as `number | bigint`. It always returns a `bigint`.
- Fixed: `@types/bun` accepted a `Buffer` or `URL` as the path in `Bun.mmap()`. Both throw at runtime.
- Fixed: `@types/bun` was missing `byteLength` on instances of `Bun.MD5`, `Bun.SHA256` and the other hash classes.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/d0831bc9fe53ceec29281fb9b7dfdebea39bc351 -->

- Fixed: `@types/bun` typed the `cpuTime` fields of a subprocess's `resourceUsage()` as `number` when they're `bigint`, and `FileSystemRouter`'s `origin` as `string` when it can be `null`.

<!-- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/3880151f0abacaf7dce9d6d0ab1c7be295d14bb4 -->
